items.title: Effectiveness of Upfront Radiotherapy in Central Nervous System Germ Cell Tumors
items.authors: Shieh CS, Liu YL, Ho WL, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Purpose: Radiotherapy (RT) is essential for curing central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS-GCTs) except for pure mature teratoma (MT), but the optimal target volume, dose, and timing remain controversial. This study evaluated the benefit of upfront RT in CNS-GCTs. Materials And Methods: We reviewed CNS-GCT patients under 30-year-old treated from 2015 to 2023. Patients with pure germinomas (PG) received whole-ventricular irradiation (WVI) with tumor bed (TB) boost. Patients with malignant non-germinomatous germ cell tumor (MNGGCT) received WVI or whole-brain irradiation (WBI) with TB boost, with or without craniospinal irradiation (CSI), before or after platinum-etoposide-based chemotherapy (CTX). Serum alpha-fetoprotein and human chorionic gonadotropin levels guided diagnosis when histopathology was unavailable. Patients with MT were treated surgically. The primary endpoint was 5-year event-free survival (EFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), neurocognitive outcomes, and endocrinopathy rates. Results: Twenty-nine patients were analyzed: 13 PGs, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront RT, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront CTX, and 2 MTs. The median follow-up of these tumors was 6.0, 6.6, 3.7, and 10.3 years, respectively. PGs receiving upfront RT achieved 5-year EFS and OS of 100% and 100%, respectively. For MNGGCTs receiving upfront RT, 5-year EFS and OS was 85.7% and 85.7%, respectively; 1 patient died from post-treatment disease progression. MNGGCTs treated with upfront CTX had 5-year EFS and OS of 41.7% and 60.0%, respectively; 2 patients relapsed (1 died), and 1 died from treatment-related complications. Both MTs remained event-free over 6 years following surgery alone or with Gamma Knife radiosurgery. Conclusions: Upfront RT provided excellent outcomes in PGs and may eliminate the need for CTX in those achieving complete response.

items.title: Lung Cancer Screening Recommendations in the Elderly: International Society for Geriatric Oncology Consensus Statement
items.authors: Steimer D, Frain L, DuMontier C, et al.
items.abstract: Introduction: Current or former smokers with a 20-pack-year history between the ages of 50 and 80 years are eligible for lung cancer screening (LCS) under current guidelines. Despite age restrictions for screening, older patients remain at risk for lung cancer and, without screening, are diagnosed with advanced-stage disease that limits curative treatment options.Treatment for early-stage lung cancer has improved with minimally invasive surgical techniques and reduced toxicity associated with stereotactic body radiation therapy. Robust older patients can tolerate surgical resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy with rates of recovery similar to those of their younger peers. Given the advancements in treatment and the improved tools available to identify frailty, chronological age should not be a gatekeeper for LCS. Methods: A taskforce within the International Society of Geriatric Oncology was created to address challenges of LCS within older patients. Taskforce members represented five different specialties with clinical expertise in lung cancer and the care of older adults. Results: For patients above 80 years old who qualify for LCS, we recommend performing a geriatric assessment (GA) to assess functional status and age-related vulnerabilities. Robust patients, as determined by GA, should be eligible for screening and discuss their health care priorities in shared decision-making conversations. GA should be performed every 2 years while patients are enrolled in LCS to determine the appropriateness of continued screening efforts. Conclusions: Age should not be an exclusion criterion for LCS. Patients above 80 years old should be thoughtfully co-managed by geriatric and lung cancer specialists to determine which older patients would benefit from screening efforts.

items.title: Safety and treatment duration of ribociclib + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a phase 3 randomized controlled trial (NATALEE)
items.authors: Rugo HS, Harbeck N, Hortobagyi GN, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The phase 3 NATALEE trial demonstrated sustained invasive disease-free survival benefit for patients with stage II or III HR+/HER2-  early breast cancer (EBC) treated with ribociclib + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (NSAI) vs. NSAI alone. Here we report detailed safety and tolerability data from NATALEE to further inform clinical decision-making. Methods: In NATALEE, men and pre- and postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2-  EBC were randomized 1:1 to ribociclib 400 mg/day (3 weeks on/1 week off; 36 months) + NSAI (anastrozole or letrozole; ≥60 months) or NSAI alone. Men and premenopausal women also received goserelin. Safety analyses included incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (AEs) as well as severity, timing, management, and outcomes. Safety parameters among older vs. younger patients were also assessed. Results: At this 45.7-month median follow-up (data cutoff: April 29, 2024), the safety analysis set comprised 4967 patients receiving ribociclib + NSAI (n = 2526) or NSAI alone (n = 2441). The most common grade ≥ 3 AEs occurring with ribociclib + NSAI vs. NSAI alone, respectively, were neutropenia (grouped term; 44.4% vs. 0.9%), liver-related AEs (grouped term; 8.6% vs. 1.7%), and leukopenia (grouped term; 8.0% vs. 0.4%). Drug-related serious AEs occurred in 2.8% vs. 0.5%, respectively. Among patients receiving ribociclib + NSAI, AE-related ribociclib discontinuation occurred in 20.2% (median onset, 4.3 months), with 9.0% of instances occurring because of liver-related AEs. AE-related ribociclib dose interruptions (66.8%; median onset, 1.8 months) and dose reductions (23.0%; median onset, 3.2 months) were primarily driven by neutropenia (dose interruptions, 43.4%; dose reductions, 14.1%). In the ribociclib + NSAI arm, AE incidence and ribociclib dose interruptions or reductions occurred at similar rates among older patients (≥ 65 years) and younger patients (< 65 years). A higher proportion of older patients permanently discontinued ribociclib due to AEs (28.1%; n = 113/402) vs. younger patients (18.6%; n = 396/2124), most commonly due to alanine aminotransferase increased (older, 8.5%; younger, 7.0%). Conclusions: Overall, ribociclib 400 mg was well tolerated, including in older patients, and AEs were manageable with current NATALEE label recommendations of dose interruptions and reductions. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03701334 (registered September 21, 2018).

items.title: Reproducibility of (18)F-FDG PET/CT-based tumour and nodal target delineation in stage II-III breast cancer
items.authors: Vinante L, Urbani M, Bampo C, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Reproducible delineation of gross tumour volumes is essential for imaging-based target definition in breast cancer, particularly in potential preoperative radiotherapy workflows. However, manual MRI-based segmentation is prone to inter-observer variability. This study explores whether 18F-FDG PET/CT, through a guideline-based semi-automated segmentation workflow, improves reproducibility for both primary tumour and nodal disease. Methods: We performed a retrospective in silico study of 30 patients with stage II-III breast cancer who underwent both contrast-enhanced MRI and 18F-FDG PET/CT before neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Two independent multidisciplinary expert groups delineated primary tumour (GTV-T) and nodal metastases (GTV-N) using manual MRI and semi-automated PET/CT (fixed 41% SUVmax threshold; EANM-compliant). Volumes were compared using paired t-tests and Bland-Altman analysis. Inter-observer reproducibility between groups was quantified using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC). Results: PET/CT-derived GTV-T volumes were consistently smaller than MRI-based volumes, reaching statistical significance in one observer group (p = 0.04). For GTV-N, mean volumes were comparable across modalities. However, PET/CT achieved superior inter-observer agreement: mean DSCs were 0.81 (GTV-T) and 0.83 (GTV-N), compared with 0.79 and 0.73 for MRI. Optimal reproducibility (DSC ≥ 0.80) was achieved in 70% of tumours and 80% of nodal volumes with PET/CT, versus 53% and 33% with MRI (p = 0.01 for GTV-N). PET/CT identified all 44 metastatic lymph nodes with 100% concordance, outperforming MRI (80%). Conclusion: An EANM guideline-based semi-automated ^18F-FDG PET/CT segmentation workflow provides more reproducible GTV delineation than manual MRI, particularly for nodal disease. Its functional target definition and supine acquisition support integration into radiotherapy workflows, including preoperative strategies requiring consistent transfer of target volumes, and may improve standardization in stage II-III breast cancer.

items.title: Reliability-weighted patch learning for synthetic CT reconstruction in head and neck adaptive radiotherapy: A proof-of-concept study
items.authors: Kim JH, Olberg S, Choi BS, et al.
items.abstract: Abstract Background Cone‐beam computed tomography (CBCT) is essential for adaptive radiotherapy (ART) but is limited by poor image quality. Existing deep learning methods for synthetic CT (sCT) generation face a critical trade‐off: diffusion models offer high fidelity but are impractically slow, while fast‐inference networks often lack structural accuracy and optimization stability. Purpose To develop HQ‐PatchNet, a reliability‐driven deep learning framework designed to improve CBCT‐to‐sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed for online ART workflows. Methods HQ‐PatchNet utilizes a vision transformer (ViT)‐integrated CycleGAN architecture. It introduces a reliability‐driven, SSIM‐based selective patch weighting mechanism controlled by a temperature decay schedule. This dynamically suppresses artifact‐dominated regions and focuses optimization on anatomically reliable structures. The model was evaluated on 304 paired head‐and‐neck (HN) scans against conventional networks and recent diffusion models using quantitative metrics (MAE, SSIM, NCC, PSNR), computational speed, and clinical dosimetric accuracy (3D gamma index, 2%/2 mm). Results HQ‐PatchNet improved image quality, reducing Mean Absolute Error (MAE) from 44.81 ± 11.24 HU to 11.85 ± 4.31 HU and achieving an SSIM of 0.960 ± 0.055, comparable to state‐of‐the‐art diffusion models. Inference required only 6.42 ± 1.71 s per volume, compared to > 15 min for diffusion approaches. The model reduced severe metal and truncation artifacts, and representative qualitative assessment suggested visually consistent sCT generation under interfractional anatomical variation. Dosimetric assessment of complex HN IMRT plans yielded a high average gamma passing rate of 99.32 ± 0.56%. Conclusions HQ‐PatchNet provides a computationally efficient and clinically promising approach for daily CBCT‐guided online ART by improving CBCT‐to‐sCT image quality while maintaining rapid inference speed. Further contour‐based, multi‐institutional, and multi‐site validation remains necessary to confirm its broader clinical utility.

items.title: Brief Report: Patterns of Disease Progression with Durvalumab versus Placebo After Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Limited-Stage SCLC in the Phase 3 ADRIATIC Trial
items.authors: Senan S, Cui H, Spigel DR, et al.
items.abstract: Introduction: In the ADRIATIC study, consolidation durvalumab significantly improved dual primary endpoints of overall and progression-free survival versus placebo for patients with limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) and no progression following concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT). We report post-hoc, exploratory analyses of patterns of disease progression. Methods: Patients were randomized to receive durvalumab, durvalumab-tremelimumab (not reported), or placebo, stratified by disease stage and prophylactic cranial irradiation use, and were treated until progression or intolerable toxicity, or for up to 24 months. First site of progression (BICR per RECIST v1.1) was classified as intrathoracic (any lesion within the lungs and mediastinum) and/or extrathoracic (lesions outside the lungs, including chest wall/diaphragm). Time to progression or death for intrathoracic progression, extrathoracic progression, and brain/central nervous system progression were assessed by Kaplan‒Meier methods. Results: In the durvalumab (n=264) and placebo (n=266) arms, 47.7% and 59.4% of patients, respectively, had progression; rates of intrathoracic-only progression were 27.7% and 29.3%. Extrathoracic lesions occurred in 20.1% and 30.1% of patients in the durvalumab and placebo arms, respectively; the most common site was the brain (6.8% and 12.4%). Time to intrathoracic progression or death (HR 0.81 [95% CI: 0.61‒1.08]) and time to extrathoracic progression or death (HR 0.68 [95% CI: 0.49‒0.93]), including brain progression or death (HR 0.64 [95% CI: 0.40‒1.01]), favored durvalumab versus placebo. Conclusion: The lower rate of extrathoracic progression and prolonged time to progression or death for intrathoracic and extrathoracic (including brain) lesions observed with durvalumab versus placebo further support consolidation durvalumab as the new standard-of-care treatment for patients with LS-SCLC without progression after cCRT.

items.title: A systematic evaluation of lattice radiation therapy: from automated vertex placement to dosimetric criteria
items.authors: Zhu X, Zhu X, Xia X, et al.
items.abstract: Objective: This study aims to establish a predictive, standardized lattice radiotherapy (LRT) workflow by systematically evaluating crystallographic close-packing strategies, formulating volume-stratified parameter guidelines, and implementing an integrated dosimetric evaluation framework. Approach: Lattice structures (4,095 configurations) were constructed across 21 patients with bulky tumours (613-1909 cm³) utilising three automated close-packing models (face-centred cubic [FCC], axial hexagonal close-packed [HCPxoy], and coronal rotated [HCPyoz]) parameterised by vertex diameter (Dlat) and the ratio of centre-to-centre distance-to-diameter (Dctc/Dlat). After evaluating geometric scaling, a representative sub-cohort spanning the volume spectrum was selected to generate 33 high-dose VMAT plans (20 Gy in 2 fractions, D0.03cc ≥ 140%). Dosimetric evaluation was conducted using global indices (PVDR1, PVDR2) and an automated 1D local gradient scoring algorithm (PVDR3, Mean ± SD). Main Results: While Dlat and Dctc/Dlat governed geometric scaling, lattice volume occupancy (LVO) and vertex count (Nlat) did not differ significantly across placement models and rotational angles (p > 0.05), indicating that geometric placement results were insensitive to placement strategies. In parameter sensitivity plans, local PVDR3 increased from 1.67 ± 0.28 to 5.41 ± 2.91 as Dctc/Dlat expanded from 2.0 to 3.5. A volume-stratified Dctc/Dlat ratio of 3.0-3.5 was optimal for ensuring geometric eligibility (1% ≤ LVO ≤ 10%) while guaranteeing steep physical gradients (PVDR3 ≥ 3.0): a ratio of 3.5 maximises local fall-off (PVDR3 = 5.41 ± 2.91) in ultra-bulky targets (>1200 cm³), whereas 3.0 is the necessary standard for medium-bulky targets (600-1200 cm³, PVDR3 = 3.05 ± 0.63). Although vertical staggering (Δz) physically reduced local dose bridging (p < 0.01), plan-level PVDR3 showed no statistically significant differences across placement models (p > 0.05). Significance: This work transitions LRT from empirical trial-and-error to a deterministic, parameter-driven framework. The proposed volume-stratified guidelines, flexible close-packing models, and automated PVDR3 scoring pipeline provide essential physical benchmarks for clinical trial standardisation.

items.title: Overall Survival in Adults With Acute Myeloid Leukemia Initiating Quizartinib vs Midostaurin With Chemotherapy
items.authors: Lee MH, Tramontano AC, Lin C, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Midostaurin and quizartinib are approved with intensive chemotherapy (IC) in patients with newly diagnosed FLT3 internal tandem duplication (ITD)-positive acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but no randomized clinical trials have directly compared them. Objective: To compare 1-year overall survival (OS) among patients with FLT3-ITD variant AML initiating IC with midostaurin or quizartinib. Design, Setting, And Participants: This multicenter, retrospective cohort study included patients with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD variant AML treated at 12 US referral centers between January 1, 2018, and May 31, 2025. Data analysis was performed from January 2026 to August 2026. Exposures: Induction therapy with IC plus midostaurin or quizartinib. Main Outcomes And Measures: The primary outcome was 1-year overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included 1-year event-free survival (EFS), induction response, and hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) rates at first remission; FLT3 clearance after induction was exploratory. Safety outcomes included rates of febrile neutropenia, infections, intensive care unit use, total parenteral nutrition and granulocyte colony-stimulating factor use, discharge to a rehabilitation facility after index hospitalization, and early mortality. Cox proportional hazards regression models were adjusted for baseline covariates and HCT as time dependent. Results: Among 215 patients (median [IQR] age, 56.0 [45.0-65.0] years; 119 [55.3%] female), 127 (59.1%) received midostaurin and 88 (40.9%) received quizartinib. Median (IQR) follow-up was 667.0 (289.0-1368.0) days for midostaurin and 324.0 (168.0-546.5) days for quizartinib, reflecting the latter's more recent approval. One-year OS was 78.0% for midostaurin and 93.0% for quizartinib (hazard ratio [HR], 0.22; 95% CI, 0.08-0.58; P = .002). The 1-year EFS was 56.0% for midostaurin and 77.0% for quizartinib (HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.25-0.74; P = .003). Patients receiving quizartinib had higher rates of composite complete remission (75 [85.2%] vs 93 [73.2%]; P = .03), whereas rates of FLT3 clearance after induction (20 [38.5%] for quizartinib vs 27 [40.3%] for midostaurin; P = .84) and HCT in first remission (47 [53.4%] for quizartinib vs 83 [65.4%] for midostaurin; P = .08) were comparable. Midostaurin was associated with higher intensive care unit use (19 [15.0%] vs 4 [4.5%]; P = .02), discharge to a rehabilitation facility (9 [7.1%] vs 1 [1.1%]; P = .04), and treatment interruptions (32 [25.2%] vs 10 [11.4%]; P = .01).…

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Remote Symptom Monitoring During Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy in Breast Cancer
items.authors: Hu X, Yang F, Curry AN, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Adjuvant endocrine therapy (AET) reduces recurrence and mortality for women with early-stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, yet long-term adherence is suboptimal, largely due to treatment-related symptoms. Remote patient monitoring (RPM) is a potential strategy to improve symptom management, but evidence of its cost-effectiveness is limited. Objective: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of RPM for women prescribed AET for early-stage breast cancer. Design, Setting, And Participants: This economic evaluation used data from the THRIVE trial, which randomized adult women initiating AET to an application (app), the app with tailored feedback, or enhanced usual care (EUC) at a large cancer center with 14 clinics from November 15, 2018, to June 11, 2021. The intervention lasted 6 months, and participants were followed up for 12 months (completed September 19, 2022). Each of the 2 interventions was compared with EUC, with uncertainty assessed using probabilistic sensitivity analyses. Data analyses were performed from February 1, 2025, to September 2, 2026. Main Outcomes And Measures: Primary outcomes included costs, which were captured during the 12-month study period from a societal perspective, including medical costs, patient time and travel costs, clinician time costs responding to alerts, and app costs; quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), derived from patient-reported 12-item Short Form Health Survey scores; incremental cost-effectiveness ratios; and incremental net monetary benefit. Results: Of 304 participants randomized, 214 had complete data. The mean (SD) age was 58.9 (10.8) years. Mean (SD) total costs were highest for the EUC arm ($11 596.10 [$30 231.95]) compared with the app arm ($6682.15 [$12 963.34]; difference, -$4913.95 [95% CI, -$12 864.27 to $3036.37]) and app plus feedback arm ($11 407.85 [$47 068.42]; difference, -$188.25 [95% CI, -$12 830.16 to $12 453.66]). The mean (SD) estimated QALYs were similar across arms (app, 0.79 [012]; app plus feedback, 0.78 [0.13]; EUC, 0.78 [0.12]). This results in an incremental net monetary benefit of $5813.95 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], -$1860.00 to $16 492.58) for app group and $88.25 (95% UI, -$14 781.73 to $13 849.34) for the app plus feedback group at $100 000 per QALY. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses suggest that the app intervention had a 68.2% to 78.1% probability of being cost-effective compared with EUC across a willingness-to-pay threshold of $0 to $200 000 per QALY, while the app plus feedback intervention had a 53.6% to 70.8% probability of being cost-effective.…

items.title: Feasibility and Tolerability of Chemoimmunotherapy Given During Induction for Treatment of Patients With High-Risk Neuroblastoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group
items.authors: Federico SM, Naranjo A, Zhang FF, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: The addition of the anti-GD2 antibody dinutuximab (DIN) to postconsolidation therapy led to improved event-free survival (EFS) for patients with high-risk neuroblastoma (HRNBL). The combination of DIN with chemotherapy (chemoimmunotherapy) results in objective responses in patients with recurrent/refractory neuroblastoma. We evaluated the feasibility of administering chemoimmunotherapy during induction for HRNBL in a multicenter trial. Methods: Children's Oncology Group (COG) ANBL17P1 was a prospective, single-arm, limited institution pilot study to assess tolerability and feasibility of administering DIN and sargramostim with induction chemotherapy cycles 3-5. The primary end point of tolerability was assessed as the occurrence of a predefined unacceptable toxicity or toxic death during DIN-containing cycles. Feasibility was assessed as ability to receive ≥75% of planned DIN doses. Revised International Neuroblastoma Response Criteria were used to assess response. Results: Forty eligible, evaluable patients with newly diagnosed HRNBL were enrolled at eight sites from January 2019 to June 2020. The most common DIN-related grade ≥3 toxicities during induction cycles 3-5 included fever (30.0%) and pain (7.5%). There were no unacceptable toxicities or toxic deaths during induction cycles 3-5. Patients received 92.0%-101.8% of intended induction DIN doses. This regimen was therefore deemed both feasible and tolerable. Thirty-seven patients completed all end-of-induction evaluations; 13 had complete response (CR), 22 partial response (PR), one minor response (MR), zero stable disease, and one progressive disease. The overall end of induction CR + PR rate was 87.5%. The 3-year EFS was 52.5% ± 7.9%. Conclusion: Administration of DIN with COG induction cycles 3-5 for patients with newly diagnosed HRNBL was tolerable and feasible. This approach is currently being evaluated in a COG randomized phase III trial.

items.title: Prognostic value of PD-L1 expression and association with HRD in high-grade serous ovarian cancer: an ancillary analysis of the PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25 trial (GINECO)
items.authors: Bataillon G, Cyrille S, Salvioni A, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The prognostic significance of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) remains uncertain, because of heterogeneity in assays, scoring systems, and assessment of tumor and immune compartments across studies. We therefore evaluated its biological and prognostic relevance using a standardized pathological approach in a large, well-annotated phase III trial cohort. Materials And Methods: In this ancillary retrospective biomarker analysis of PAOLA-1/ENGOT-ov25, PD-L1 was assessed by 22C3 pharmDx immunohistochemistry on whole-slide sections from 324 International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage III-IV HGSOCs. Three predefined scoring systems commonly used in PD-L1 assessment were applied: tumor proportion score (TPS ≥1%), immune cell score (IC ≥1%), and combined positive score (CPS ≥1). Associations with homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), BRCA1/2 status, and survival were examined using multivariable Cox models adjusted for major clinicopathological factors. Results: PD-L1 positivity was observed in 38.2% of tumors by TPS, 62.4% by IC, and 66.1% by CPS. Positivity did not significantly vary by sampling site or timing of tissue collection relative to chemotherapy. PD-L1 positivity was enriched in HRD-positive tumors (TPS: 42.3% versus 28.0%, P = 0.017; IC: 65.1% versus 52.0%, P = 0.030; CPS: 70.4% versus 53.0%, P = 0.003) and remained independently associated with improved overall survival in adjusted analyses [TPS: adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.70 (95% confidence interval 0.49-1.00), P = 0.046; IC: aHR 0.68 (0.49-0.95), P = 0.025; CPS: aHR 0.70 (0.50-0.97), P = 0.037]. Associations with progression-free survival were not statistically significant after adjustment. Conclusions: In advanced HGSOC, standardized whole-slide PD-L1 assessment identifies an HRD-associated PD-L1-positive immune context independently associated with improved overall survival. Immune-integrated scoring approaches capture this signal more effectively than tumor-cell-restricted assessment and provide a robust framework for future ovarian cancer studies.

items.title: Pembrolizumab plus FLOT as neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapy in locally advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancer: analysis of the FLOT cohort from the phase 3 KEYNOTE-585 study
items.authors: Al-Batran SE, Shitara K, Folprecht G, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Results from the third interim analysis of the phase 3 KEYNOTE-585 study (NCT03221426) showed superior pathological complete response (pCR) with perioperative pembrolizumab and chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab versus placebo plus chemotherapy, then adjuvant placebo in locally advanced, resectable gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; differences in event-free survival (EFS) were not statistically significant. We present results from a complementary cohort that evaluated pembrolizumab plus fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) versus placebo plus FLOT. Patients And Methods: KEYNOTE-585 is a randomized, phase 3 study conducted at 143 medical centers. Participants were randomly assigned 1 : 1 to pembrolizumab plus FLOT or placebo plus FLOT. In this exploratory cohort, the primary endpoint was safety. Post hoc exploratory endpoints included pCR rate per the Mandard scale by blinded independent central review, EFS per RECIST v1.1 by investigator, and overall survival (OS). Results: Overall, 203 participants were randomly assigned (pembrolizumab group, n = 100; placebo group, n = 103). Median time from randomization to data cut-off (16 February 2024) was 43.8 months (range, 36.5-69.8). Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse event rates were 72.7% and 62.1%, respectively. Treatment-related deaths occurred in three participants (3.0%) in the pembrolizumab group and one participant (1.0%) in the placebo group. The pCR rate was 17.0% [95% confidence interval (CI), 10.2-25.8] in the pembrolizumab group and 6.8% (95% CI, 2.8-13.5) in the placebo group. Median EFS was not reached (NR; 95% CI, 28.2-NR) versus 31.6 months (95% CI, 22.8-NR), respectively [hazard ratio (HR) 0.75, 95% CI 0.50-1.13]. Median OS was NR in either group (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.53-1.25); 36-month OS rates were 66.0% and 59.2%. Conclusion: Neoadjuvant/adjuvant pembrolizumab plus FLOT was feasible and showed an acceptable safety profile. Exploratory efficacy endpoints showed numerical trends consistent with those of the main cohort in locally advanced resectable gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.

items.title: Translating absolute risk of breast cancer into screening frequency: a framework to guide practice
items.authors: Jiang S, Bennett DL, Rosner B, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Current precision mammography screening trials use heterogeneous risk models, risk strata, and screening intervals, with no consensus on how absolute breast cancer risk should translate into screening frequency. A standardized, risk-model-agnostic approach could improve consistency in trial design and facilitate broader clinical implementation. To develop and evaluate a risk-model-agnostic framework that maps guideline-defined absolute breast cancer risk cut points to screening intervals that can guide the design of future personalized screening strategies and translate smoothly to routine clinical practice. Methods: Screening interval and frequency derived from the absolute risk of breast cancer in US women is the main outcome. Results: The framework yielded a gradient of estimated screening intervals that scaled with absolute risk: annual (2%-3%); annual with supplemental imaging/counseling (≥3%); biennial (1%-2%); and potentially less frequently. When compared with ongoing intervention trials, screening intervals assigned by trials varied widely and were not uniformly aligned with absolute-risk levels, underscoring the lack of standardized mapping between risk and screening intensity. Conclusion: A risk-model-agnostic framework based on absolute-risk cut points can provide a transparent and standardized method for specifying screening intervals in personalized mammography screening. This approach may improve consistency in future intervention trials and facilitate equitable implementation of precision screening across population settings.

items.title: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort
items.authors: McSorley ST, Iwata T, Ammar A, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk. Methods: Patients undergoing polypectomy within the Scottish Bowel Screening Programme, with surveillance colonoscopy between 6 months and 6 years were included (n = 2642). Chromogenic immunohistochemistry (IHC; n = 2466), 6-plex multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n = 331), and spatially resolved 6000-plex single cell transcriptomics (n = 7) were applied to adenoma microarrays. Cell density and location were measured using QuPath. Hierarchical then K-means clustering was used to define immune cell density-based clusters, which were compared to future lesion events using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log rank test. Results: After adjustment for age, sex, site, size and dysplasia, adenoma CD3+ T cell density was significantly associated with future colorectal neoplasia (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.20-1.72, p < 0.001). Using mIF, three immune cell density clusters were identified; 1) high T cell density, low macrophage density, 2) low T cell density, low macrophage density, and 3) high T cell, macrophage and αSMA density, with significant differences in future lesion risk (Cluster 1: 22%, Cluster 2: 41%, Cluster 3: 36%, p = 0.032). Bulk RNAseq and spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed significant variation in T cell and macrophage co-location and gene expression profiles between clusters. Conclusion: Adenoma immune contexture emerges as a possible determinant of future metachronous lesion risk, offering a novel biomarker to refine surveillance.

items.title: Impact of sexological follow-up on the sexual function of patients treated with chemo-radiotherapy and brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer: results of the prospective FEMINICOL study
items.authors: Menard J, Lusque A, Attal J, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Purpose: Radiotherapy and brachytherapy (BT) for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) are associated with high rates of sexual morbidity, particularly vaginal stenosis. The prospective FEMINICOL study assessed sexual function and vaginal toxicity in patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and image-guided adaptive BT, with systematic sexological support. Materials And Methods: This single-centre prospective cohort study (NCT03956498) included patients treated with concomitant CRT and BT between October 2019 and December 2020. A certified sex therapist met each patient before BT, at 2 months and 1 year after treatment. The primary objective was to evaluate sexual function one year after treatment using the FSFI questionnaire. Results: Sixty patients were included in the study. Among patients who received clinical follow-up (54 at 2 months and 47 at 1 year), compliance with sexological follow-up was 98.1 % (53/54) at two months and 100 % at one year. Fifty-six patients with baseline evaluation and at least one post-treatment evaluation were analyzed. Median age was 54.5 years (31-77). At one year, 55.3 % of patients adhered to vaginal rehabilitation and 45.7 % were sexually active. Median FSFI score improved from 4 (range: 2-33.2) at baseline to 12.5 (2-34.8) at 1 year (paired test p < 0.001). Median sexual activity (QLQ-CX24) increased from 0 (0-66.7) to 33.3 (0-100) at 1 year (p < 0.001), while sexual anxiety remained stable (p = 0.93). At 1 year, Grade ≥ 3 vaginal toxicity occurred in 12.7 % of patients, mainly narrowing (8.5 %). Most patients (81.4 %) were satisfied with the sexological support. Conclusion: In this prospective cohort, systematic sexological support during and after CRT and BT was feasible and was associated with encouraging compliance with vaginal rehabilitation and favorable sexual function outcomes over time.

items.title: Quantitative and mutational properties in the ctDNA uncovered by systemic inflammation in large B-cell lymphoma
items.authors: Arffman M, Meriranta L, Bonsdorff A, et al.
items.abstract: Risk assessment of large B-cell lymphomas (LBCLs) using liquid biopsy (LB) has so far focused primarily on the genomic properties of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), overlooking the host response. We previously identified an inflamed serum protein signature that reflects systemic host response and correlates with survival. Here, we integrated the inflammation signature and ctDNA to connect inflammation to genomic alterations and defined how this crosstalk informs treatment outcomes in two independent LBCL cohorts from Nordic phase II trials. We identify initiation of immune evasion at multiple genomic levels in patients with an inflammatory serum profile and uncover distinct mutational signatures that reflect diagnostic subtypes and inflammatory host response. We describe the added prognostic value of multimodal LB assessment, where patients with high levels of both ctDNA and inflammatory serum proteins have the worst overall survival (hazard ratio 7.93, p < 0.001) and progression free survival (hazard ratio 5.35, p < 0.001), thereby improving the risk estimate compared to either of the markers alone. This advanced multimodal LB employs clinically critical information on lymphoma and the host, both of which are essential for accurate treatment decision-making.

items.title: Depletion of CD19-positive B-cells and dexamethasone premedication may result in immune suppression in patients with B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia after consolidation treatment with blinatumomab
items.authors: Zugmaier G, Goekbuget N, Luger S, et al.
items.abstract: Treatment of patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) has benefited greatly from the introduction of different immunotherapy approaches targeting CD19 or CD22. In particular, when added to or when replacing some parts of chemotherapy treatment, blinatumomab, a bispecific T-cell engager which creates an immunological synapse between patient's CD3-expressing T lymphocytes and CD19-positive cells, including leukemia blasts, has shown unprecedented efficacy in preventing leukemia relapse/progression in both adults and children with either newly diagnosed or relapsed B-ALL. Despite the great anti-leukemia efficacy shown by blinatumomab, data obtained in large randomized studies in adults and children with newly diagnosed B-ALL have shown that the benefit of immunotherapy has, in part, been offset by an increased risk of infections, which can even occur long after completion of immunotherapy. Blinatumomab is also able to lyse normal B lymphocytes, and the resulting long-lasting, profound B-cell aplasia may lead to severe hypogammaglobulinemia, in turn increasing the incidence of infectious complications. Premedication with dexamethasone is widely used for mitigation of neurotoxicity and other systemic toxicities related to initial exposure to blinatumomab, but the dose usually employed does not derive from well-conducted studies aimed at identifying the recommended steroid dose. In addition, there is no robust evidence of a neuroprotective effect of Dexamethasone. This Spotlight Review aims to highlight the importance of monitoring immunoglobulin levels and to provide guidelines for initiation and continuation of immunoglobulin replacement therapy. In addition, we focus on need to conduct studies properly addressing the identification of optimal corticosteroid doses, regimens, and timing.

items.title: Salvage High-Dose-Rate Brachytherapy for Localized Prostate Cancer Recurrence: A Comparative Analysis of 2 Fractionation Schedules-Single-Institution Study of 223 Patients
items.authors: Stankiewicz M, Wilk A, Krzempek M, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Salvage high-dose-rate brachytherapy (sHDR-BT) is an effective option for radiorecurrent prostate cancer. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and toxicity of two sHDR-BT fractionation schedules and identify factors associated with treatment outcomes. Methods And Materials: We retrospectively analyzed 223 patients treated with sHDR-BT between 2008 and 2021. Patients received either 3 × 10 Gy (n = 150) or 2 × 13 Gy (n = 73). Median follow-up was significantly longer in the 3 × 10 Gy group (125 vs 79 months, P < .001). Apart from a higher frequency of high-grade disease (P = .02) and nodal/distant recurrence (P < .001) in the 2 × 13 Gy cohort, baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups. The Kaplan-Meier estimator, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards models were used in statistical analysis. Results: In the entire cohort, the 5-year overall survival rate exceeded 75%, and the median biochemical control was 12.6 years. Factors independently associated with worse oncological outcomes included primary International Society of Urological Pathology grade 5, nodal or distant recurrence, castration resistance, and shorter interval from primary therapy to recurrence. Use of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) reduced the risk of local failure (P = .04). Late genitourinary and gastrointestinal toxicity was acceptable and comparable between the subgroups (P = .6 and P = .4, respectively). In the no-ADT subgroup (n = 83), median overall survival was 113 months, and median ADT-free survival reached 88 months. Conclusions: Regardless of the fractionation schedule, sHDR-BT is an effective option for selected patients with localized, noncastration-resistant recurrence, characterized by relatively low toxicity. Castration resistance and regional or distant metastases strongly limit efficacy. In appropriately selected patients, salvage therapy can substantially delay the initiation of ADT.

items.title: Comparative evaluation of plan robustness in proton and photon radiotherapy in deep inspiration breath-hold for mediastinal lymphomas throughout the treatment course
items.authors: Hörberger F, Enmark M, Andersson KM, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Purpose: Proton therapy (PT) is sensitive to anatomical changes and setup uncertainties, which can compromise dose robustness in the treatment of mediastinal lymphoma, an issue less pronounced with photon-based radiotherapy. Variations in target position and size can potentially influence plan robustness. This study evaluated the robustness of pencil beam scanning (PBS) PT versus volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) photon treatment plans across sub-target volumes and organs of interest (OOI) in deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) throughout treatment. Material And Methods: Twenty-eight patients with upper mediastinal lymphoma treated with PBS-PT in DIBH were included. Clinically delivered PBS-PT plans were retrospectively compared with VMAT plans optimized per institutional standard-of-care. All plans were recalculated on weekly verification computed tomography images (vCTs) to assess target coverage and OOI doses. The internal target volumes (ITV) were subdivided into mediastinum, fossa supraclavicularis, neck, axilla and, along with OOIs, transferred from planning CTs to the vCTs. Results: In the nominal plans, PBS-PT generally achieved lower OOI doses than VMAT, an advantage maintained on the vCTs. Both modalities demonstrated robust target coverage and OOI sparing. ITVTotal coverage fell below the set criterion (D98% > 95%) on at least one vCT for six patients with PBS-PT, but only one patient for VMAT. Pronounced deviations (D98% < 90%) occurred for two PBS-PT cases. Sub-target robustness was generally good. Conclusions: Both PBS-PT and VMAT were robust for mediastinal lymphoma treatment in DIBH. In a proton-eligible DIBH cohort, PBS-PT provided superior OOI sparing, while VMAT demonstrated greater consistency in target coverage.

items.title: Treatment plan quality comparison between ZAP-Axon(®) Krylov optimizer and Leksell Gamma Knife(®) Lightning optimizer for brain metastasis
items.authors: Lee YC, Maslowski A, Kotecha R, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: This study compares stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) treatment plan quality between the recently launched ZAP-Axon® Krylov optimizer and the Leksell Gamma Knife® (LGK) Lightning optimizer for brain metastasis (BM). Methods: Thirty (n = 30) patients who were previously treated with LGK SRS or fractionated SRS were selected and divided into three groups: large post-operative resection cavities of BM (BMlg, postop), large intact BM (BMlg, intact) and small intact BM (BMsm, intact). Based on our institutional planning guidelines, the 30 clinical cases were replanned using ZAP-Axon Krylov and LGK Lightning optimizers without manual adjustments. Statistical analysis was performed to compare plan quality metrics (Paddick conformity index [PCI], gradient index [GI], target coverage [TC], prescribed isodose line [Rx IDL], and treatment time/scaled beam-on-time [sBOT] [min]) between the two optimizers. Results: For the BMlg, postop group, mean values of PCI, GI, TC, Rx IDL, and treatment time/sBOT (min) for Krylov versus Lightning plans were 0.91 versus 0.91, 2.48 versus 2.56, 99.5% versus 99.7%, 51.1% versus 53.7% and 37.4 min versus 36.5 min, respectively. All metrics except for the Rx IDL (%) were not statistically significantly different. For the BMlg, intact group, corresponding values were 0.93 versus 0.93, 2.42 versus 2.57, 99.5% versus 99.7%. 51.5% versus 53.0% and 35.9 min versus 36.3 min. While GI was statistically significantly different (p <0.05) between the two optimizers, the rest of the metrics were not. For the BMsm, intact group, corresponding values were 0.71 versus 0.64, 3.10 versus 3.26, 99.5% versus 99.5%, 61.9% versus 53.0% and 8.1 min versus 19.8 min. In this group, PCI and treatment time/sBOT were statistically significantly different (p <0.05), whereas GI and Rx IDL were not. Conclusion: Without manual adjustments, ZAP-Axon Krylov plans were comparable to LGK Lightning plans for large BM lesions, but the Krylov optimizer outperformed the Lightning optimizer for small BM lesions.

items.title: A virtual physicist framework integrating dose prediction and large language models for automated treatment planning
items.authors: Zhu H, Li J, Liang Y, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Automated radiotherapy treatment planning has benefited from data-driven approaches; however, achieving consistently high plan quality across patients remains challenging. Dose prediction models provide patient-specific priors but lack adaptive optimization, whereas large language models (LLMs) offer strong reasoning capabilities but raise concerns regarding stability and safety in clinical use. Purpose: To develop and validate a fully automated VMAT treatment planning framework integrating dose prediction and LLM-driven dynamic optimization, termed the Virtual physicist (VP), and to evaluate its dosimetric performance, plan complexity, and consistency relative to manual and other automated planning strategies. Methods: A total of 70 cervical cancer patients previously treated with VMAT were retrospectively collected. The dataset was divided into 50 cases for training, 10 for validation, and 10 for testing. The input data consisted of patients' planning CT images with contoured planning target volumes (PTVs) and organs at risk (OARs). The outputs included predicted three-dimensional dose distributions (upper-, middle-, and lower-dose bands) and automatically generated VMAT treatment plans with corresponding dosimetric and plan complexity metrics. The VP framework was implemented in the MOZI treatment planning system via a Python scripting interface. A dose-band prediction model was used to initialize patient-specific optimization constraints. During optimization, an LLM iteratively adjusted objectives and weights based on real-time dosimetric feedback, subject to a rule-based safety engine enforcing clinical and physical constraints. Plans generated using dose prediction only (DP-only), LLM only (LLM-only), and combined dose prediction with LLM (DP + LLM) were compared with clinically delivered manual plans. Results: The DP + LLM strategy significantly improved sparing of the bladder and bilateral femoral heads compared with all three other strategies and significantly reduced rectal doses relative to the DP-only and manual plans (P < 0.05), while maintaining PTV Dmean, HI, CI, and GI comparable to those of the manual plans (P > 0.05). For dual-layer MLC plan complexity, DP + LLM produced a more balanced modulation pattern than manual planning, with lower distal-layer complexity-significant for d-C/A and d-MCS but not d-BA-and higher proximal-layer complexity across all three metrics.…

items.title: Local Therapy of Metastases in Colorectal Cancer: Utilization and Survival in a Nationwide Population
items.authors: Ystgaard MF, Myklebust TÅ, Lassen K, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Local therapy (LT) for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is recommended when eradicating all metastases is feasible. Although LT is widely used, its population-level impact remains unclear. This study aims to use real-world population-based data to assess LT utilization and survival trends in mCRC. Methods: Patients diagnosed with mCRC from 2010 to 2023 were included, using data from the Cancer Registry of Norway and the Norwegian Patient Registry. LT was defined as surgery, stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT), or ablation targeting liver, lung, or brain metastases. Outcomes were reported as median overall survival (OS) and 2-, 5-, and 10-year OS. The effect of the first versus last time period on survival was assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression. Results: Among 64,112 CRC cases, 20,210 had mCRC. Of these, 21% received LT, 39% systemic therapy only, 12% other therapies, and 29% no therapy. Metastasectomy was the primary LT (87%), whereas SRT use was limited. LT use increased by 12% annually from 2010 to 2015 and then stabilized. The overall mCRC survival improved, with the 5-year OS increasing from 16% to 23% and the median OS from 15 to 18 months (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.95). No significant survival improvement was observed between time periods in the LT or systemic therapy only subgroups. The 5-year OS for patients receiving LT for liver, lung, and brain metastases was 50%, 62%, and 5%, respectively. Conclusion: LT utilization increased, with outcomes comparable with more selected populations. Survival in treatment subgroups remained stable over time, but improved in the overall mCRC population, suggesting that the population-level gains may reflect changes in treatment allocation rather than improvements within modalities.

items.title: Identifying novel genomic alterations in relapsed childhood B-ALL: a report from the Children's Oncology Group
items.authors: Feng Y, Li H, Mulder HL, et al.
items.abstract: Relapsed B-acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) generally occurs due to the emergence of subclones resistant to therapy, leading to poor outcome. Here, we describe novel genomic alterations responsible for therapeutic resistance at a subtype level in a clinical trial (AALL1331) which randomized patients to blinatumomab and chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone. We performed whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing on 288 patients (183 diagnosis/first relapse/germline trios and 105 additional patients with first-relapse samples) and analyzed 41 second-relapse samples. For ETV6::RUNX1, we showed that cases with gain of the fusion allele or with fusion transcript involving exon 5 of ETV6 and exon 4 of RUNX1 (E5-E4) had a higher risk of first relapse than cases with E5-E3. For the hyperdiploid subtype, we demonstrated that low modal chromosomal numbers (51-52) were more prone to first relapse than those with ≥53 chromosomes, with an additive effect of CREBBP mutations. We showed enrichment of IKZF1 alterations in the Philadelphia-like subtype and that NSD2 E1099K was commonly associated with relapse in TCF3::PBX1. Together, these new features accounted for 30% (n=55) of first relapses. Intriguingly, ~3% of relapses are related to secondary B-ALL or germline predisposition. We also compared genomic alterations at diagnosis and first relapse in relation to second relapse status in randomized patients, with TCF3::PBX1/NT5C2 linked to worse outcomes regardless of randomized arm. Together, our findings provide novel insights into the genomics of relapsed childhood B-ALL as well as in the context of blinatumomab therapy. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as # NCT0201853.

items.title: Glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression-a marker of resistance to cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors
items.authors: Gu Y, Ruan L, Hou Y, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Resistance to cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors remains a major clinical challenge in treating estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, with no reliable predictive biomarkers currently available for patient selection. Methods: To investigate resistance mechanisms, we generated drug-tolerant persisters to abemaciclib and palbociclib in a panel of estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer cell lines. Clariom D human transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify differentially expressed genes, and the data were compared with published data from the PEARL (Phase III study of palbociclib plus endocrine therapy versus capecitabine in patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer resistant to aromatase inhibitors) clinical trial to verify the clinical relevance. The impact of stable glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression in sensitive cells was studied in in vitro and in vivo xenograft models. Results: Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4 and 6 inhibitor-resistant drug-tolerant persisters exhibited G1 arrest and demonstrated increased senescence. Transcriptomic profiling of drug-tolerant persister models identified 154 genes consistently associated with resistance across cell lines. In the comparison with published resistance-associated genes from the phase III PEARL trial, glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B was a strongly upregulated candidate in both datasets. Glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression in sensitive cells conferred resistance to CDK 4 and 6 inhibition, enhanced migratory capacity, and accelerated tumor progression, abrogating the growth-inhibitory effects of abemaciclib observed in control tumors. Across all treatment arms, glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression tumors failed to respond to CDK 4 and 6 blockade. Glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression increased the expression of integrins, including integrin beta 1 (ITGB1) and integrin alpha 5 (ITGA5), and activated protein kinase B (AKT) and extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) signaling, as evidenced by elevated phospho-AKT (Ser473) and phospho-ERK 1 and 2 (Thr202/204). Treatment of glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression cells with the antibody-drug conjugate glembatumumab vedotin, as a single agent, potently decreased cell viability. Additionally, strong synergy with abemaciclib was observed.…

items.title: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Delirium Risk
items.authors: Friedman JI, Parchure P, Fu W, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Although external validation of machine learning (ML)-based delirium risk models is a key stage in the model development pipeline, few published reports exist. Moreover, ML-based delirium risk models commonly degrade in performance during external validation. Objective: To examine the performance of a fusion multimodal with natural language processing (NLP) delirium risk stratification model in live clinical practice with cross-hospital external validation. Design, Setting, And Participants: This quality improvement study evaluated live clinical deployment of the model among patients 60 years or older who were admitted to non-intensive care units at Mount Sinai Hospital (MSH), with external validation performed at Mount Sinai Morningside Hospital (MSM), from December 1, 2024, to December 31, 2025. Main Outcomes And Measures: Primary outcomes were performance of the risk stratification model, assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), and monthly delirium detection rates. A 2 × 2 confusion matrix was created, and the 4 cells were used to calculate model performance metrics and compare associated diagnostic yield between premodel deployment and active model deployment periods. Results: The overall sample included 33 095 admissions to non-intensive care units at MSM and MSH (mean [SD] age, 74.86 (9.22) years; 15 601 women [47.1%], 17 271 men [52.2%]). A total of 9020 MSM inpatient admissions were assigned a delirium risk score by the risk stratification model during live clinical operations and were compared to 21 186 MSH inpatient admissions that were assigned a risk score by the same model. Age at admission significantly differed between patients at MSM and MSH (MSM: median [IQR] age, 75.79 [68.25-83.88] years vs MSH: 72.62 [66.64-79.65] years; P < .001). Patients from MSM and MSH also significantly differed by sex, race and ethnicity, surgical vs medical primary diagnosis, length of stay, and dementia prevalence rate. Among 11 909 MSM patients, patients in the pre-ML cohort (median [IQR] age, 78.00 [71.00-85.00] years) were significantly older than those in the post-ML cohort (median [IQR] age, 75.79 [68.25-83.88] years) (P < .001). The AUROC of the model was 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90-0.92) for MSM and 0.94 (95% CI, 0.93-0.94) for MSH. The positive predictive value of the model was 25.9% for MSM and 19.4% for MSH. For MSM, the mean monthly delirium detection rate significantly increased from 9.23% (95% CI, 8.07%-10.38%) to 19.59% (95% CI, 17.32%-21.85%) after model deployment (P < .001).…

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA Profiling Across Phase II/III Ewing Sarcoma Trials Identifies High-Risk Patients With TP53, STAG2, and CDKN2A Alterations
items.authors: Mous L, Ballet S, Dureau S, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Ewing sarcoma is an aggressive bone cancer driven by FET::ETS fusions, with few recurrent secondary genomic alterations (most commonly involving STAG2, TP53, and CDKN2A) and copy-number variants. Currently, diagnosis relies exclusively on tumor biopsies and imaging, and despite a well-defined genomic landscape, risk stratification remains based solely on clinicoradiologic parameters. Furthermore, tumor evolution and intrapatient heterogeneity remain poorly characterized, and prospective evidence supporting molecular risk stratification is limited. Materials And Methods: We prospectively integrated serial circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) sampling into the first-line phase II/III Euro Ewing 2012 (EE2012) and CombinaiR3 trials, complemented by relapse studies. Across 347 patients, 991 blood, tumor, and bone marrow samples were profiled using custom targeted sequencing and shallow whole-genome sequencing to enable integrated biologic characterization and clinical correlative analyses. Results: ctDNA recapitulated established Ewing sarcoma genomic landscapes while also revealing intrapatient tumor heterogeneity when compared with matched tumor biopsy profiles. Blood and bone marrow plasma profiles were highly concordant. Longitudinal sampling identified selection of TP53-altered clones at relapse. Clinically, detection of TP53 and/or STAG2 loss-of-function mutations and/or CDKN2A focal deletions in ctDNA at diagnosis predicted poor outcomes and, in a multivariable model adjusting for metastatic status, tumor volume, age, and treatment, defined an independent molecular high-risk subgroup with inferior event-free survival (hazard ratio [HR], 3.6 [95% CI, 2.2 to 5.8], P < .001) and overall survival (HR, 4.3 [95% CI, 2.5 to 7.3], P < .001) in EE2012 patients. Conclusion: Prospective, trial-integrated ctDNA profiling provides comprehensive molecular characterization, reveals clinically relevant heterogeneity and clonal evolution, and identifies an independent molecular high-risk subgroup at diagnosis, supporting ctDNA-guided risk stratification in Ewing sarcoma.

items.title: Cancer in the Commonwealth: a Lancet Oncology Commission
items.authors: Atun R, Sirohi B, Jaffray D, et al.
items.abstract: Cancer is now one of the defining health and development challenges of our time. The 56 nations of the Commonwealth, home to 2·7 billion people, mirror this global burden. Recorded cancer cases across member states rose by 35% in 2008-18 and the number of deaths reached almost 1·7 million in 2018. The Lancet Oncology Commission on cancer in the Commonwealth was convened to ask a deceptively simple question: how can 56 diverse nations act collectively to close the widening gap between the burden of cancer and the capacity of each country to respond? 80 researchers, clinicians, policy makers, and civil society members, organised into five working groups and ten research streams, spent 2 years assembling the evidence base for this report. Using a validated microsimulation model, we estimate that 5-year net survival across eleven common cancers in the Commonwealth stood at just 30·7% in 2020, ranging from 4·1% in low-income countries (LICs) to 59·0% in high-income countries (HICs), driven overwhelmingly by late-stage presentation, which affects 62% of patients in LICs compared with 43% in HICs. This difference in survival is compounded by chronic underinvestment. Infrastructure gaps are equally stark: only 12% of countries meet international benchmarks for CT imaging, 22% for hospital density, and 40% for radiotherapy. Governance is underdeveloped too: barely one-third of Commonwealth countries have a national cancer control plan meeting basic quality criteria. Research investment also mirrors these inequities: between 2016 and 2023, Commonwealth countries collectively invested only US$165 per cancer-related disability adjusted life year. Yet the case for investment is unambiguous. Our modelling shows that a comprehensive scaleup of treatment, imaging, and quality of care could raise 5-year net survival across the Commonwealth from 30·7% to 52·9%, averting an estimated 5·8 million deaths and adding 113 million life-years between 2025 and 2035, at an incremental cost of $36·7 billion, delivering a return of between four and twenty dollars on every dollar invested. Crucially, this investment need not depend chiefly on external aid, which is contracting sharply at present. Our modelling for 38 low-income and middle-income Commonwealth countries suggests that up to $701 billion in additional domestic fiscal space could be mobilised between 2025 and 2030, through budget reprioritisation, macroeconomic growth, targeted taxation, and prudent borrowing. On this evidence, the Commission proposes six priority actions.…

items.title: Activity and safety of first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial
items.authors: Zhang J, Shi Y, Zhang Q, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Pumitamig, an investigational bispecific antibody targeting programmed death ligand-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, has shown preliminary efficacy across several tumour types. We aimed to evaluate the safety and activity of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. Methods: In this single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial conducted at ten sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in China, patients aged 18-75 years with histologically documented, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and one or more measurable lesion (as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1) received first-line pumitamig (20 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. In phase 1b, six patients received pumitamig (20 mg/kg once every 2 weeks intravenously plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) and were monitored for treatment-emergent adverse events, before subsequent enrolment in phase 2. The primary endpoints were confirmed objective response rate and safety, assessed in the efficacy-evaluable population, defined as all patients who received one or more doses of study drug and had measurable disease at baseline and at least one efficacy assessment. This trial is registered with chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2200060400) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05918133), and is closed to recruitment. Findings: Between June 27, 2022, and March 15, 2023, 42 patients were enrolled, received one or more doses of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel (median duration of exposure 9·0 months, 95% CI 6·9-11·7) and had one or more tumour assessments. All patients were Chinese and female; median age was 53 years (IQR 41-60). At a median follow-up of 35·2 months (95% CI 33·0-36·1), the confirmed objective response rate was 73·8% (95% CI 58·0-86·1; 31 of 42 patients), including one complete response and 30 partial responses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were decreased neutrophil count (13 [31%] of 42 patients), decreased white blood cell count (11 [26%]), proteinuria (six [14%]), and febrile neutropenia (five [12%]).…

items.title: Treatment-related neutropenia as predictor of response to adjuvant palbociclib in the PALLAS trial (ABCSG-42/AFT-05/BIG-14-13/PrE0109)
items.authors: Fanucci K, Dueck AC, Mayer EL, et al.
items.abstract: Abstract Background Prior analyses of PALLAS (NCT02513394), a phase III trial that randomized patients with stage II-III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer to receive adjuvant palbociclib plus endocrine therapy (ET) or ET alone, did not show benefit of the combination. Separate data show extent of treatment-related neutropenia is associated with improved response to palbociclib and other cell cycle-specific therapies. We conducted an exploratory analysis to assess whether grade of treatment-related neutropenia could identify benefit from palbociclib in the adjuvant setting. Methods Patients receiving palbociclib were classified into those with treatment-emergent high-grade neutropenia (HGN) with maximum grade ≥3 (absolute neutrophil count <1000/mm 3 ), or low-grade/no neutropenia (LGN) with maximum grade ≤2. These groups were compared to each other and to the ET-alone group for 5-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS). Results 5736 patients were included: 2840 in the palbociclib+ET arm and 2896 in the ET-alone arm. Patients receiving palbociclib+ET consisted of 1006 (35.4%) LGN and 1834 (64.6%) HGN. Lower body mass index (BMI), Asian race, prior chemotherapy, and mastectomy were associated with HGN (all p < 0.05). Patients receiving ET alone had inferior 5-year iDFS compared with patients who developed HGN by cycle 6 on palbociclib+ET (hazard ratio [HR] 1.19, 95% confidence interval [CI]:1.01-1.40; p = 0.04), an association that persisted after adjustment for prior chemotherapy, race, and BMI (HR 1.20, 95% CI:1.02-1.42; p = 0.03). Conclusion In this exploratory analysis of the PALLAS trial, palbociclib+ET showed benefit over ET alone in patients who developed HGN in the first 6 treatment cycles. Neutropenia could be a useful biomarker for palbociclib efficacy. Trial registration clinicaltrials.gov, NCT02513394

items.title: Dasatinib in pediatric patients with chronic myeloid leukemia in chronic phase: long-term efficacy and endocrine analysis
items.authors: Samis J, Patterson BC, Gore L, et al.
items.abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) accounts for 2-3% of childhood leukemias. CA180 226 is a prospective phase 2 trial evaluating dasatinib in pediatric patients with newly diagnosed (ND) or imatinib resistant/intolerant (IM R/I) chronic phase CML (CML CP). Analyses showed rapid molecular responses, but long term efficacy, deep molecular responses (DMR), and endocrine effects of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in children have not been reported. This study reports long term outcomes in the largest pediatric cohort to date with endocrine assessment during TKI therapy. ND patients received dasatinib tablets (Cohort 3A) or oral suspension (Cohort 3B), while IM R/I patients were enrolled in Cohort 1. Cohorts 3A and 1 received 60 mg/m² daily; Cohort 3B received 72 mg/m² daily. Median follow-up was 94.8 months for Cohort 3 and 92.4 months for Cohort 1. Height z scores declined over the first few years of therapy particularly in prepubertal children, whereas BMI and bone density changes were mild. Thyroid and gonadal abnormalities were infrequent. Major molecular responses (MMR) occurred within the first 2 years, with 96 month MMR rates of 83.3% in Cohort 3 and 69.0% in Cohort 1. DMR accumulated, with MR4 and MR4.5 rates of 54.8% and 41.7% in Cohort 3 and 37.9% and 27.6% in Cohort 1 at 96 months, respectively. Median progression free and disease free survival were not reached. These long-term data demonstrate durable dasatinib efficacy to induce DMR alongside initial height z-score decline and modest additional endocrine effects, providing important insight into TKI therapy in pediatric CML-CP. items.title: Salvage-free, transplantation-free survival: a proposal for a new clinical endpoint in acute myeloid leukemia
items.authors: Récher C, Bérard E, Tavitian S, et al.
items.abstract: Results from pivotal clinical trials evaluating the combination of intensive chemotherapy with targeted therapies in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) are expected soon. While overall survival (OS) or event-free survival (EFS) are the recommended endpoints, new criteria are needed for assessing the intrinsic effectiveness of new drugs. In this study, the salvage-free, transplantation-free survival (STFS) was measured from day 1 of induction chemotherapy to the date of induction failure or salvage therapy, allogeneic transplantation (allo-HSCT), relapse, or death from any cause, whichever occurs first and assessed in a cohort of 1966 AML patients from the DATAML registry treated with intensive chemotherapy and 100 acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) patients treated with arsenic trioxide and all-trans retinoic acid. Validation cohorts from the ALFA group were used. At five years, STFS was estimated at 14.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 13.0-16.2; median, 5.5 months) whereas OS, EFS and relapse-free survival estimations were 40.4% (95% CI, 38.2-42.6; median, 30.6 months), 31.4% (95% CI, 29.4-33.5; median, 15.3 months) and 37.6% (95% CI, 35.2-40.0; median, 21.9 months), respectively. Relapse was the most common first STFS event, followed by allo-HSCT. STFS varied depending on molecular subgroups and gene-gene mutation interactions. In the APL cohort, STFS (83.6% at five years) was similar to OS (85.6%) illustrating the impact of an effective and low-toxicity first-line treatment curing patients without salvage therapy or allo-HSCT. In the prospective randomized ALFA-0701 trial, gemtuzumab ozogamycin significantly improved STFS. STFS should complement other survival endpoints to accurately analyze the impact of new drugs in AML.

items.title: Patient-Provider Communication, Treatment, and Survival in a Population-Based Cohort: The North Carolina-Louisiana Prostate Cancer Project
items.authors: Wang JH, Song L, Carmichael BDM, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Patient-provider communication (PPC) may be associated with receipt of definitive prostate cancer treatment and long-term outcomes. We examined these associations in a racially and geographically diverse population-based cohort. Methods: We analyzed data for 2,258 Black and White participants enrolled in the North Carolina-Louisiana Prostate Cancer Project (2004-2009), with longitudinal vital status follow-up through 2020. PPC was measured using three subscales: contextual knowledge, communication content, and interpersonal treatment. We evaluated associations between PPC and receipt of definitive treatment and clinical outcomes. Results: Communication content emerged as the most consistent PPC domain associated with clinical outcomes. Per five-point increase in communication content, the odds of receiving definitive treatment were higher for radiation therapy (odds ratio [OR], 1.49 [95% CI, 1.15 to 1.94]) and radical prostatectomy (OR, 1.73 [95% CI, 1.39 to 2.14]) compared with nondefinitive treatment. Communication content was also associated with greater likelihood of surgery within 3 months among prostatectomy recipients (OR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.29 to 2.13]), with a directionally similar but nonsignificant association for radiation therapy. In competing-risk models, higher communication content was associated with lower prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM; subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 0.78 [95% CI, 0.61 to 0.99]). Associations varied by race and rurality, but formal interaction tests did not indicate effect measure modification. Conclusion: We found that higher communication content scores were associated with higher receipt of definitive treatment, shorter time to surgery, and lower PCSM. These findings highlight communication as a potentially modifiable component of the patient-provider encounter. Communication based on high informational quality is associated with long-term prostate cancer outcomes and represents a candidate target for future intervention research to improve prostate cancer care delivery.

items.title: Experimental verification of clinical dose and LET maps for LET-informed proton therapy
items.authors: Jensen ML, Van Heerden M, Stolarczyk L, et al.
items.abstract: Objective:Linear energy transfer (LET)-informed proton therapy has the potential to improve biological treatment planning beyond the conventional, constant-RBE assumption. Its clinical translation, however, requires experimental tools capable of verifying spatially resolved dose and dose-averaged LET (LETD) distributions under clinically relevant conditions. We recently introduced an optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) film-based detector system that simultaneously measures two-dimensional (2D) absorbed dose and LETD. This work provides a first assessment of the system for verifying dose and LETDdistributions from clinical proton therapy plans.Approach:The system was tested at two proton therapy centers, ranging from simple uniform fields to more complex geometries, including Bragg curve measurements and a clinically realistic anthropomorphic head phantom treatment plan. Measured dose and LETDdistributions were compared against commercial treatment planning system (TPS) calculations and, for selected fields, to external Monte Carlo particle transport simulations due to the absence of traceability of LETD. For non-uniform irradiations, agreement was assessed using gamma analysis with 3%/2 mm and 5%/2 mm criteria for dose and LETD, respectively.Main results:For uniform fields, measured dose and LETDdistributions generally agreed with TPS and independent Monte Carlo simulations across a range of clinically relevant irradiation conditions. In the Bragg curve measurement, gamma pass rates were 96.6% for dose and 99.7% for LETD, with the largest dose discrepancy observed near the Bragg peak, consistent with a current over-correction of detector quenching in high-LET regions to be improved in future work. In the anthropomorphic phantom, gamma pass rates ranged from 75% to 100% for dose and from 45% to 95% for LETD, with a single layer showing a sub-50% pass rate for LETD. Failing regions were confined to high-dose superior layers for dose and distal-edge, high-LET regions for LETD.Significance:The presented results support the detector system's use as an experimental benchmarking tool for TPS-calculated dose and LETDmaps. Given this and the system's ability to simultaneously measure 2D dose and LETDmaps with high spatial resolution and minimal field perturbation, the system shows promise for future commissioning workflows for LET-informed proton therapy.

items.title: Deep learning-based automated segmentation of target volumes for pediatric craniospinal irradiation in proton therapy
items.authors: Kim SH, Oh G, Kim JY, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Accurate target delineation is essential for achieving optimal plan quality in craniospinal irradiation (CSI), particularly in pediatric proton therapy. However, manual target delineation is highly time-consuming due to the large anatomical extent of craniospinal axis. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a deep learning-based automated segmentation model to streamline the target delineation for pediatric proton CSI. Methods: Fifty pediatric patient datasets treated with proton CSI at the National Cancer Center Korea were utilized. The nnU-Net v2 framework was employed for model training using 40 datasets, with the remaining 10 used for independent evaluation. Segmentation performance was assessed using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Intersection over Union (IoU), 95th percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95), and Average Symmetric Surface Distance (ASSD). Workflow efficiency was evaluated by comparing manual and automated contouring times, and clinical acceptability was assessed using a Likert scale. Results: The model achieved high geometric accuracy, with mean DSC, IoU, HD95, and ASSD values of 0.9587, 0.9222, 2.4948 mm, and 0.7900 mm, respectively. The target delineation time was reduced from approximately 8 h to 30 min. Clinical acceptability was favorable, with the majority of Likert scale ratings falling within the positive-to-neutral range. Conclusions: This study demonstrates that the developed deep learning-based automated segmentation model can achieve accurate and robust target delineation for proton CSI. By integrating this framework into the planning workflow, CSI can be performed with greater efficiency, reproducibility, and standardization. Our findings highlight the potential of automation to advance precision and productivity in pediatric proton CSI practice.

items.title: Combining handcrafted radiomics features and deep learning features within different regions of interest in planning CT images for the prediction of symptomatic radiation pneumonitis in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer
items.authors: Li X, Hang H, Kong Y, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To predict symptomatic radiation pneumonitis (RP) in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC) patients by handcrafted radiomics (HCR) and deep learning (DL) features of three different regions of interest (ROIs) in normal lung tissue. Methods: Ninety LA-NSCLC patients from Center A were collected as the development cohort, and an additional 57 patients from Center B were collected as the external validation set. Clinical data and lung dose-volume parameters were collected from the patients, and univariate analysis was conducted. Three ROIs in lung were delineated in pre-radiotherapy CT images: Lung-PTV, Lung-GTV, and PTV-GTV. For each ROI, 1046 HCR features and 512 DL features were respectively extracted, and then correlated. For each ROI, three models (HCR, DLR, and a hybrid model) were developed with feature selection via Spearman correlation, mRMR, the LASSO method, and SVM-based modeling. And finally, their performance was evaluated and compared using AUC values from ROC curves. The optimal model was selected by comparing the best AUC through internal validation results, and then external validation was conducted. Calibration and decision curve analyses were used to evaluate the model. Results: In the development cohort, univariate analysis revealed no statistically significant associations with RP. The correlation analysis revealed a weak correlation between HCR and DL features. In internal validation, for Lung-PTV, Lung-GTV and PTV-GTV, HCR models achieved AUCs of 0.658 (95%CI: 0.645-0.671), 0.659 (95%CI: 0.646-0.672), and 0.890 (95%CI: 0.881-0.899); DLR models obtained AUCs of 0.832 (95%CI: 0.824-0.840), 0.900 (95%CI: 0.893-0.907), and 0.777 (95%CI: 0.766-0.788); and the hybrid model showed AUCs of 0.838 (95%CI: 0.831-0.846), 0.901 (95%CI: 0.894-0.908), and 0.919 (95%CI: 0.912-0.926). The results showed that the DLR model outperformed the HCR model for Lung-PTV and Lung-GTV, and the hybrid model surpassed both for all three ROIs. The hybrid model of PTV-GTV was found to be the best, and its external validation was conducted. The results showed that the AUC for the external validation set was 0.828 (95%CI: 0.696-0.960). The model was well calibrated (p > 0.05), and decision curve analysis indicated positive net benefit across relevant threshold probabilities. Conclusions: Hybrid models combining HCR and DL features showed the highest predictive performance in internal comparisons and the best-performing PTV-GTV hybrid model was externally validated, highlighting the potential of combined features for improved prediction.
