items.title: Pelvic bone marrow dosimetry predicts grade ≥ 2 hematologic adverse events in locally advanced rectal cancer
items.authors: Li L, Hong Y, Lin Z, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Hematologic adverse events (HAEs) are common in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) undergoing neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT), potentially leading to treatment interruptions and compromised efficacy. This study aimed to develop a hematologic adverse event prediction model using volumetric dose parameters. Methods And Materials: All doses were converted to the equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions (EQD2) using an α/β ratio of 10 Gy for bone marrow. Pelvic bone marrow (PBM) was contoured, and dosimetric parameters (DmeanEQD2, V3EQD2-V40EQD2) were analysed. The association between ≥ 2 grade HAE (HAE2+) and dosimetric/clinical parameters was evaluated through logistic regression. The normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model was constructed through logistic regression analysis of HAE2+. The PBM dosimetric threshold was determined through receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. The predictive performance of the model was internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Results: Of the 141 patients, 49 (34.8%) developed HAE2+. In multivariate analysis, DmeanEQD2 and V40EQD2 were associated with HAE2+ (all P < 0.05). In the NTCP analysis, the dose levels corresponding to a 50% probability of HAE2 + were 24.2 Gy for DmeanEQD2 and 13.3% for V40EQD2. ROC analysis identified optimal thresholds of DmeanEQD2 ≤ 24.09 Gy (AUC = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.70-0.86) and V40EQD2 ≤ 13.00% (AUC = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.76-0.90) for predicting HAE2+. Conclusion: In LARC patients receiving nCRT, the dose limitation of PBM DmeanEQD2 ≤ 24.09 Gy and V40EQD2 ≤ 13.00% may reduce the risk of HAE2+. These findings provide quantitative dosimetric references for pelvic bone marrow protection and may help reduce the risk of moderate-to-severe hematologic adverse events. items.title: Optimizing Access in Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy as a Resource-Efficient Alternative to Conventional Schedules
items.authors: Jacinto AA, de Melo AGV, Rovina AAS, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Concomitant chemoradiation therapy (cCRT) is a standard-of-care treatment option for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, improving locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS). However, many patients are unfit for cCRT and receive sequential chemoradiation therapy (sCRT); in this setting, hypofractionated radiation therapy may reduce treatment time, counter tumor repopulation, and improve access. Methods And Materials: We retrospectively analyzed outcomes and prognostic factors among 131 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated at a single high-volume cancer center with 1 of 3 approaches: cCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-C; n = 52), sCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-S; n = 37), or sCRT with hypofractionation (HYPO-S; n = 42). Results: After a median follow-up of 19.6 months, OS, progression-free survival, and distant failure-free survival were comparable among groups. LRC was significantly higher with HYPO-S (62.0%) than with CONV-S (34.8%; p = .009) and similar to CONV-C (62.0%). In multivariate analysis, LRC with HYPO-S remained comparable to CONV-C (p = .576), whereas CONV-S was associated with inferior LRC compared with HYPO-S (hazard ratio, 2.257; 95% CI, 1.046-4.867; p = .038). Toxicity profiles were acceptable, with no significant differences in rates of grade ≥2 esophagitis or pneumonitis across groups. Conclusions: Sequential hypofractionated chemoradiation therapy achieved LRC and OS comparable to cCRT and superior LRC compared with sequential conventional schedules, without increased toxicity. These findings support broader adoption of HYPO-S as a resource-efficient, clinically effective strategy for patients ineligible for cCRT, particularly in low-income and middle-income health care systems.

items.title: Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Cadaveric Study
items.authors: Tanabe S, Yoshio K, Komiyama T, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Hydrogel spacers reduce the rectal radiation dose and toxicity in prostate cancer radiation therapy. However, their use in other malignancies, including renal cell carcinoma (RCC), remains underexplored. This study aimed to explore the feasibility of hydrogel spacer placement at different retroperitoneal sites and its potential dosimetric effects during stereotactic body radiation therapy for RCC using cadaveric models. Methods And Materials: Hydrogel spacers were percutaneously administered under computed tomography (CT) guidance to 3 cadavers at the following retroperitoneal sites: (1) the perirenal space, (2) the perivascular region of the iliac vessels, and (3) the iliacus muscle region. Spacer stability and separation distance from organs at risk were evaluated using CT images acquired immediately after placement, at 1 week, and at 1 to 2 months. The dosimetric effect was assessed in the perirenal spacer case by comparing radiation treatment plans for a simulated RCC lesion generated before and after spacer placement using a treatment planning system. Results: Hydrogel spacer placement in the perirenal space achieved a stable separation of approximately 1 cm between the kidney and bowel, which was maintained at the 1-month follow-up. The perivascular spacer failed to maintain its shape at the time of placement and became indistinguishable on the follow-up CT, whereas the iliacus muscle spacer remained stable but provided limited bowel separation. Treatment planning showed a reduction in bowel dose in the perirenal case, with the maximum dose to the small intestine reduced by 9.6% and to the large intestine by 35.9%. Conclusions: This exploratory cadaveric study suggests that CT-guided hydrogel spacer placement in the perirenal space may be technically feasible and may reduce the bowel dose in simulated RCC stereotactic body radiation therapy. However, the other retroperitoneal locations evaluated in this study showed less favorable spacer behavior or limited bowel separation. Further studies are required to validate these preliminary findings.

items.title: Deep learning-based self-supervised detection and localization of magnetic resonance imaging anomalies in artificial intelligence-supported radiotherapy workflows
items.authors: Kadhim M, Rogowski V, Persson E, et al.
items.abstract: Background and purpose: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into radiotherapy workflows, yet it remains vulnerable to out-of-distribution image data that can introduce unexpected behavior in clinical tasks. Deep learning (DL)-based anomaly detection for pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains limited and transparent evaluation for full automation is lacking. This study aimed to develop two self-supervised anomaly-detection framework variations in radiotherapy for pelvic and brain MRI. Materials and methods: A two-stage self-supervised DL-framework was trained separately for pelvic and brain MRI utilizing three public datasets. The first stage compressed normal image data into discrete representations, and a second stage modeled the representation distribution. Anomaly-evidence was obtained by combining perceptual image differences with token-surprisal scores via negative log-likelihood estimation. Automated detection was evaluated for two anatomical cohorts: pelvis, encompassing both synthetic global anomalies and real clinical anomalies, and brain, comprising clinically annotated anomalies. Performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). For each cohort, a subset of normal images was reserved for analysis. Results: Promising exploratory performance across evaluation cohorts was obtained. AUCs were 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.99) for synthetic pelvic anomalies, 0.95 (95% CI 0.90-1.00) for clinical pelvic anomalies, and 0.81 (95% CI 0.74-0.87) for brain anomalies. Qualitative heatmap analysis showed spatial agreement between detected anomalies and reference annotations. Conclusions: The framework variations showed promising anomaly detection performance across pelvic and brain MRI, supporting its potential for automated MRI quality control in radiotherapy. Heatmap-based visualization further improved interpretability by spatially localizing detected anomalies.

items.title: Metastasis-directed therapy in addition to definitive locoregional radiotherapy for De novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective cohort study
items.authors: Laskar SG, Kumar A, Malhotra R, et al.
items.abstract: Background: De novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (mNPC) carries a poor prognosis with systemic therapy alone. Locoregional radiotherapy (LRRT) improves survival in chemotherapy-responsive patients, but the incremental role of metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) remains undefined. Methods: This retrospective cohort included 54 patients with de novo mNPC treated between 2013 and 2024 at a tertiary cancer centre. All received platinum-based induction chemotherapy followed by definitive LRRT; selected patients underwent MDT to metastatic sites. Overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS) and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier methods, with Cox regression for univariable and multivariable analysis. Results: At a median follow-up of 27 months, 2-year OS, RFS and DRFS were 67.5%, 45.4% and 52.7%. MDT was associated with improved 2-year OS (92.3% vs 55.2%; p = 0.0069), RFS (81.9% vs 28.2%; p < 0.001) and DRFS (93.8% vs 35.0%; p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis MDT remained associated with improved RFS (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.08-0.98; p = 0.047), with consistent estimates in a 2-month landmark analysis (HR 0.26, 95% CI 0.075-0.90) and with MDT modelled as a time-varying covariate (HR 0.17, 95% CI 0.040-0.76); the association with OS was not statistically significant (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-1.13; p = 0.072). Oligometastatic disease was more frequent among patients receiving MDT (88% vs 41%). The association was most evident in the oligometastatic subgroup. In exploratory analyses, detectable post-treatment plasma EBV DNA and elevated post-LRRT PET SUV were associated with inferior survival. Conclusion: In chemotherapy-responsive de novo mNPC treated with definitive LRRT, consolidative MDT was associated with improved disease control in multivariable, landmark and time-varying analyses, with a directionally consistent but non-significant association with OS. As residual confounding cannot be excluded, these findings support prospective evaluation in selected patients.

items.title: Personalized biomarker-based treatment strategy in patients with recurrent/metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck: Results of the biomarker-driven cohorts of the EORTC-HNCG-1559 trial (UPSTREAM)
items.authors: Galot R, Le Tourneau C, Licitra L, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Patients with platinum-refractory recurrent/metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (R/M SCCHN) have poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Given the molecular heterogeneity of SCCHN, the biomarker-driven UPSTREAM umbrella trial evaluated personalized targeted therapies based on tumor molecular profiling. Methods: UPSTREAM enrolled patients with post-platinum R/M SCCHN. Fresh tumor biopsies underwent molecular profiling to assign patients to five biomarker-defined cohorts. Cohorts B1-B4 included p16-negative disease: B1 evaluated afatinib in tumors with EGFR and/or HER2 amplification/mutation or high PTEN expression; B2 evaluated afatinib in cetuximab-naïve patients; B3 evaluated palbociclib in CCND1-amplified tumors; and B4 evaluated niraparib in platinum-sensitive disease. B5 evaluated niraparib in p16-positive oropharyngeal carcinoma. B1-B3 were randomized against physician's choice, with 16-week progression-free survival rate (PFSR16W) as the primary endpoint; B4-B5 were single-arm studies with 16-week objective response rate (ORR) as the primary endpoint. Results: Among 250 patients enrolled across five European countries, 152 were assigned to a biomarker-driven cohort. Only B1 met its primary endpoint. In B1, 38 patients received afatinib, with a PFSR16W of 34.2%. Slow recruitment limited B2 to eight patients, with a PFSR16W of 12.5%. In B3, PFSR16W was 16.7% (n = 12). ORRs with niraparib were 3.6% (1/28) in B4 and 6.1% (2/33) in B5. Conclusion: UPSTREAM demonstrated the feasibility of a biomarker-driven umbrella trial in R/M SCCHN, but clinical activity of the evaluated targeted therapies was modest. Findings likely reflect the absence of robust oncogenic drivers, limited biomarker validation, and restricted efficacy of single-agent targeted therapy. Improved biomarker selection, next-generation targeted treatments, and rational combinations are needed to advance precision medicine in R/M SCCHN.

items.title: PELICAN-IPC 2015-016/Oncodistinct-003: A randomized non-comparative phase II study of pembrolizumab in combination with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in HER2-negative inflammatory breast cancer
items.authors: de Nonneville A, Lerebours F, Zemmour C, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a rare and aggressive disease with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options, particularly in HER2-negative disease. The role of pembrolizumab combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in IBC remains unclear. Methods: PELICAN was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, non-comparative phase II trial in HER2-negative IBC. Patients were randomized 1:2 to neoadjuvant epirubicin/cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel alone (Arm A) or with pembrolizumab (Arm B). The primary endpoint was centrally assessed pathological complete response (pCR; ypT0/is, ypN0) in Arm B. Secondary endpoints included local pCR, safety, and exploratory biomarker analyses. Results: Between August 2018 and June 2022, 54 patients were randomized and 53 received study treatment (20 Arm A, 33 Arm B). In the modified intention-to-treat population, centrally assessed pCR was 12.5% in Arm B (4/32; 90% CI, 4.4-26.4), including 6.3% in endocrine receptor-positive and 18.8% in triple-negative tumors. In Arm A, pCR was 35.0% overall (22.2% and 45.5%, respectively). No consistent association was observed between pCR and baseline PD-L1 expression, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, or circulating tumor cell-based biomarkers. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events occurred in 69.7% of Arm B and 65.0% of Arm A patients; immune-related toxicities were consistent with the known pembrolizumab safety profile. Conclusions: Pembrolizumab combined with neoadjuvant EC-paclitaxel showed limited pCR activity in HER2-negative IBC. Exploratory biomarker and early time-to-event analyses did not identify subgroups deriving clear benefit. Further translational studies are warranted to investigate resistance mechanisms and biomarker-informed therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Robustness of proliferation-based constrained spatiotemporal fractionation under setup and radiobiological uncertainties in liver radiotherapy
items.authors: Ma M, Zhang K, Chen X, et al.
items.abstract: Abstract Background Spatiotemporal fractionation redistributes dose between fractions and may reduce normal‐tissue exposure. Its sensitivity to setup uncertainty and radiobiological assumptions requires evaluation before clinical use. Purpose To evaluate proliferation‐based constrained spatiotemporal fractionation (p‐cSTF) under geometric and radiobiological perturbations in conventionally fractionated liver radiotherapy. The focus was normal‐liver dose. Methods Thirty‐five patients with hepatocellular carcinoma were included. Uniform fractionation, proliferation‐based spatiotemporal fractionation (p‐STF), and p‐cSTF were evaluated over 25 fractions. The primary comparison matched nominal mean gross tumor volume (GTV) biologically effective dose (BED); a supplementary comparison matched nominal model‐derived tumor control probability (TCP). Setup tests comprised 18 single‐axis offsets (± 1, ± 2, and ± 3 mm) and 24 transverse voxel offsets, each held constant over treatment. Thirty scenarios varied biological‐model parameters; precision checks used two 480‐scenario sequences. Nominal dose grids were evaluated under perturbations without reoptimization. Endpoints included physical dose, BED, equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions (EQD2), coverage, and response‐model scores. Results Under biological‐parameter variation, normal‐liver (liver excluding GTV) BED was 26.22 ± 7.00 Gy for p‐cSTF, 28.18 ± 7.57 Gy for Uniform, and 28.05 ± 7.76 Gy for p‐STF. Corresponding EQD2 values were 14.92 ± 3.96, 16.05 ± 4.29, and 15.96 ± 4.39 Gy. Values are cohort means and between‐patient standard deviations of patient‐specific scenario means. Normal‐liver BED remained lower with p‐cSTF after nominal TCP matching, although fixed transverse offsets produced lower GTV TCP than with Uniform. Expanded sampling retained the direction of the liver‐dose difference; the original 30 scenarios did not meet the specified precision criteria for scenario variability. Conclusions P‐cSTF retained a simulated normal‐liver dose advantage under the tested perturbations, including after nominal TCP matching. This advantage must be considered alongside target‐response trade‐offs and uncertainty in scenario‐variability estimates. Clinical toxicity and treatment deliverability were not evaluated.

items.title: Impact of correlated PBPK parameters on intra-patient global sensitivity analysis in molecular radiotherapy
items.authors: Yousefzadeh-Nowshahr E, Hardiansyah D, Vasic V, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models integrated into digital twins provide a robust framework for optimizing individualized molecular radiotherapy (MRT). Nevertheless, uncertainties in PBPK-model-derived dosimetry can compromise the reliability of dosimetry-guided treatment planning and individualized therapy decisions. Purpose: This study employs intra-patient global sensitivity analysis (GSA) to assess the influence of uncertainty and correlations among PBPK model parameters on estimated kidney and tumor absorbed doses (ADs) in prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted theragnostics. Methods: Data from 10 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who underwent pre-therapeutic [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-I&T PET/CT and a cycle of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-I&T therapy, followed by post-therapeutic SPECT/CT scans at Days 1 and 4 post-injection, were analyzed. A previously established whole-body PBPK model for PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy was used as the baseline model. Fifteen model parameters, their standard errors, and inter-parameter correlations were estimated by fitting to measured time-activity data and subsequently evaluated using intra-patient GSA based on the Kucherenko method implemented in UQLab. In one approach, correlations were ignored to identify the direct influences of uncertainty in input parameters on ADs. In a second approach, correlations were included to reflect realistic parameter distributions and to capture indirect effects arising from parameter interdependencies. Pharmacokinetics were simulated to estimate therapeutic kidney and tumor ADs as well as main- and total-effect indices (  S i , S i T )   . Sensitivity indices, ADs, and their associated uncertainty metrics were compared between scenarios with and without parameter correlations. Results: Including parameter correlations in the GSA yielded kidney ADs of 4.2 Gy [3.0-7.2 Gy] (median [min-max]) with standard deviations (SDs) of 0.5 Gy [0.4-0.9 Gy] and tumor ADs of 10.1 Gy [2.0-26.8 Gy] with SDs of 1.7 Gy [0.6-3.4 Gy]. Neglecting correlations resulted in significantly higher uncertainties in ADs, by a factor of 1.2 [1.0-1.8] for both kidneys and tumors. Kidney ADs were most sensitive to kidney receptor density (  S i = 0.3  [ 0.1 -  0.6 ] ,   S i T = 0.7  [ 0.6 - 0.8 ]   ) and to the filtered fraction of renal blood flow ( S i = 0.2  [ 0.1 - 0.3 ] ,   S i T = 0.3  [ 0.1 - 0.4 ] )   . Tumor ADs were most affected by tumor receptor density (  S i = 0.7  [ 0.1 - 1.0 ] ,   S i T = 0.8  [ 0.3 - 1.0 ]   ).…

items.title: Explainable machine learning with wavelet-enhanced multi-scale texture analysis of diabetes-related heel pad ultrasound texture differences
items.authors: Ji X, Li Y, Guo J, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Diabetes is associated with structural and functional differences in plantar soft tissues, which may be reflected in ultrasound texture patterns. However, existing ultrasound texture studies are limited by single-scale feature extraction and limited feature-level interpretability. Purpose: To develop an explainable machine learning framework incorporating a wavelet-enhanced multi-scale texture feature extraction module (WEMS-TFE), and to investigate whether heel pad ultrasound texture features differ between patients with diabetes without active foot ulcers and healthy controls. Methods: Heel pad ultrasonography was performed in 76 patients with diabetes (without active foot ulcers) and 47 healthy controls. Ultrasound images of the heel pad were analyzed at the microchamber and macrochamber levels. The WEMS-TFE module was proposed to extract multi-scale, multi-directional texture features via two-dimensional discrete wavelet decomposition combined with the gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM). Features with significant between-group differences were selected and evaluated across seven machine learning classifiers using repeated cross-validation with participant-disjoint data partitions. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret feature contributions in a representative XGBoost model. Results: The WEMS-TFE scheme achieved the highest cross-model composite performance and robustness among the five evaluated feature extraction schemes. Cross-classifier importance analysis identified 6 features that recurred across multiple classifiers. Consistently, most of these also ranked among the important features in the XGBoost SHAP analysis, and two representative features showed clear value-dependent contribution patterns. The identified features therefore reflected group-associated image-texture differences, although their associations may be affected by residual demographic confounding. Conclusions: The proposed framework, with the WEMS-TFE module as its core component, enables quantitative characterization of group-associated differences in heel pad ultrasound texture features. The findings provide imaging-based evidence of group-level texture differences in the heel pad and support further investigation of plantar tissue characteristics in diabetes, while acknowledging that these differences may be affected by residual demographic confounding and do not establish diabetes-specific structural changes or causal tissue mechanisms.

items.title: Development of a phantom-based end-to-end QA workflow for online adaptive radiotherapy incorporating high-resolution 2D detector measurements
items.authors: Niedling J, Schindhelm R, Cervantes L, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Online adaptive radiotherapy (oART) accounts for anatomical changes by adjusting treatment plans on a daily basis. However, comprehensive plan-specific quality assurance (QA) is challenging, as pre-treatment measurements cannot be performed with the patient on the treatment couch. Therefore, an end-to-end QA approach, covering imaging, contouring, plan adaptation, dose calculation, and delivery, is essential to ensure accurate and reliable oART. Purpose: To develop and evaluate an end-to-end QA workflow for oART, incorporating high-resolution detector-based 2D dose verification and interchangeable phantom inserts. Methods: A novel QA workflow was implemented using the myQA® SRS phantom with a 2D CMOS detector and a 3D-printed anthropomorphic pelvis insert. A virtually deformed planning CT was generated to simulate anatomical changes and used as input for the adaptive workflow. The process included CBCT acquisition, manual contour adaptation, plan generation, dose delivery, and comparison of measured and calculated dose distributions via Gamma Analysis. Workflow feasibility was tested through repeated measurements. Error detectability was evaluated by altering gantry/collimator angles, monitor units (MU), phantom positioning, and CBCT presets. Confidence limits, calculated following AAPM TG-119 methodology, were used as plan-specific thresholds for evaluating Gamma Pass Rates (GPR). Corresponding dose-volume histogram (DVH) parameters, using D98% for the planning target volume (PTV) and V95% for organs at risk (OARs), were calculated. Results: Ethos auto-contouring did not perform reliably on the phantom geometry, necessitating manual contouring. All workflow repetitions produced high GPR values for 3 %/2 mm, 2 %/2 mm, 3 %/1 mm, and 2 %/1 mm global criteria between measured and calculated dose. Confidence limits served as effective thresholds for identifying plan deviations. Introduced errors, including gantry angle deviations > 3° and collimator angle deviations ≥ 3°, MU variations ≥ 3 %, incorrect CBCT presets, and 3 mm setup shifts, were clearly detectable across all criteria. Smaller deviations, such as 1° angular changes or 1 % MU variation, resulting in minor dosimetric effects residing at or below 1.2 % for the PTV and 5.6 % for OARs, yielded GPR values above the Confidence limit. Conclusions: The proposed workflow is feasible, reproducible, and capable of reliably identifying plan-specific deviations in Ethos oART.…

items.title: Endovascular brachytherapy using (125)I seeds strand combined with transarterial chemoembolization, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with hepatic vein tumor thrombus
items.authors: Li M, Wan JC, Zhang W, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of Iodine-125(125I) seed strand implantation in combination with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), lenvatinib, and camrelizumab for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) with hepatic vein tumor thrombus (HVTT). Methods And Materials: From January 2020 to December 2023, 76 uHCC patients with HVTT were included in this single-center retrospective study. Thirty-six patients underwent 125I seed strand implantation combined with TACE, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab (group A), whereas 40 patients received TACE combined with lenvatinib and camrelizumab (group B). Outcome measures comprised with technique success rate, overall response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS) time, progression-free survival (PFS) time, and adverse event occurrence rate. Results: The technique was successfully performed in all patients. The mean intended dose (r, irradiation range = 10 mm; z, irradiation duration = 240 days) was 64.0 ± 0.3 Gy. No grade 3 or 4 adverse events related to 125I seed strand implantation occurred in group A. The ORR and DCR of HVTT were significantly higher in group A compared with group B (ORR, 72.2% vs. 15.0%, p < 0.001; DCR, 88.9% vs. 35%, p < 0.001). And the median OS time and PFS time were significant longer in group A compared with group B (OS, 22.1 ± 2.4 vs. 14.0 ± 1.7 months, p < 0.001; PFS, 17.6 ± 0.3 vs. 8.0 ± 0.6 months, p < 0.001). In the multivariate Cox regression analysis, treatment regimen was an independent prognostic factor for OS. No serious complications related to interventional treatment, including acute hepatic failure, liver abscess, intraperitoneal bleeding, and radiation hepatitis was observed. Conclusions: 125I seeds strand combined with TACE, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab as the treatment strategy for uHCC patients with HVTT is safe and effective.

items.title: Estimating the clinical benefit of metastases resection in liver-limited metastatic colorectal cancer: an IPD-based pooled analysis of nine randomized trials
items.authors: Germani MM, Taravella A, Rossini D, et al.
items.abstract: Background: In resected liver-limited metastatic colorectal cancer (LL-mCRC), disease-free survival (DFS) and postsurgical overall survival (psOS) have been found to be weakly related in heterogeneous retrospective series, challenging the role of DFS as a surrogate biomarker of psOS. Additionally, it remains unclear whether early relapses (DFS <6 months) are associated with overall survival (OS) benefit. Patients And Methods: We analyzed individual data of patients with LL-mCRC enrolled in nine randomized trials of first-line chemotherapy plus biologics. Correlation and surrogacy between DFS and psOS were calculated with ρ and R2. psOS of resected patients with DFS <6 months was compared with time from minimum disease load (post-min OS) of unresected patients, with stratification according to baseline tumor burden score (TBS). Time on systemic therapy was also evaluated. Results: Eight hundred fifty-five patients with LL-mCRC were included and 357 (42%) were radically resected. DFS and psOS were highly correlated (ρ = 0.73), with R2 at the patient and trial levels for surrogacy of 0.70 and 0.32, respectively. psOS and post-min OS in resected patients with early relapse (n= 115) and unresected patients (n = 498) were comparable [hazard ratio (HR) 0.88, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.70-1.11, P = 0.29]. However, a benefit from surgery was detected in patients with high baseline TBS (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.45-1.05, P = 0.09) but not in patients with low/medium baseline TBS (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.74-1.69, P = 0.59) (p interaction = 0.10). Resection was associated with a lower percentage of time on systemic therapy (26%) regardless of DFS (47% if <6 months, 26% if ≥6 months) (P < 0.001). Conclusions: In LL-mCRC resected after first-line chemotherapy plus biologics, DFS is highly correlated with psOS, with high patient-level surrogacy. In high-burden patients, liver surgery seems associated with a trend toward long-term benefit, also after early relapse (<6 months), whereas time on systemic therapy is reduced.

items.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Maternal Health Outcomes in Pregnant and Postpartum Individuals: A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.authors: Norell EM, Yue X, Mane H, et al.
items.abstract: Importance: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly used to support maternal health, but randomized evidence is limited. Objective: To evaluate whether access to a generative AI maternal health chatbot improved 12-month maternal health outcomes. Design, Setting, And Participants: This 2-group randomized clinical trial enrolled 400 participants from October 2023 to December 2024, with 12-month follow-up completed in December 2025. Participants were recruited online across 49 US states and the District of Columbia. Eligible participants were English-speaking, aged 14 years or older, pregnant or parenting an infant younger than 6 months, and self-identified as members of racial and/or ethnic minoritized groups. Interventions: Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive access to the chatbot or an active control consisting of monthly children's books. Main Outcomes And Measures: Primary outcomes were anxiety and depression symptoms at 12 months measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Secondary outcomes included emergency department visits, pregnancy-related complications, postpartum care checkups, effective contraception use, and sleep duration. Results: Among 400 randomized participants, the mean (SD) age was 32.6 (5.1) years; 200 (50%) were parenting an infant at enrollment; and 10 (2%) identified as American Indian or Alaska Native, 80 (20%) Asian, 188 (47%) Black or African American, 57 (14%) multiracial, and 65 (16%) Hispanic or Latino. The AI chatbot was not associated with differences in anxiety scores (adjusted mean difference, 0.10; 95% CI, -0.77 to 0.96) or depression scores (adjusted mean difference, -0.23; 95% CI, -1.05 to 0.59), nor with emergency department visits, postpartum care, contraception use, or sleep duration. Among participants pregnant at enrollment, the chatbot was associated with more self-reported pregnancy-related complications in the secondary 12-month end point analysis, but not in longitudinal analyses. Higher chatbot engagement was associated with longer sleep duration and higher anxiety scores in exploratory within-group analyses. Conclusions And Relevance: In this randomized clinical trial of pregnant and postpartum individuals from racial and ethnic minoritized groups, access to a generative artificial intelligence maternal health chatbot did not improve maternal anxiety or depression at 12 months compared with an active control. Secondary and exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously.…

items.title: A European multicenter cohort study of patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer receiving stereotactic body radiotherapy for non-spinal bone metastases
items.authors: Nägler F, Schäfer S, Seiler I, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is increasingly used for the treatment of bone metastases (BoM) of oligometastatic prostate cancer. This study aims to provide new information on SBRT for non-spinal BoM of oligometastatic prostate cancer in a large multicenter cohort. Methods: Retrospective data from 20 European centers on patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer who received SBRT for BoM between 2010 and 2024 were analyzed to assess patterns of practice, efficacy, safety, and prognosis. Results: A total of 317 patients with 401 BoM were analyzed. The SBRT was delivered in 1-10 fractions, with a median fractional dose of 8 Gy (range 4.0-22.0 Gy) and a corresponding total prescribed dose of 18.0-50.0 Gy. Median follow-up was 25.4 months. Local control at 1 and 3 years was 98.0% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 95.2%-99.1%) and 93.3% (95% CI: 88.1%-96.2%). Progression-free survival (PFS) rates after 1 and 3 years were 74.2% (95% CI: 67.5%-79.6%) and 44.1% (95% CI: 36.0%-51.9%). Overall survival (OS) at 1 and 3 years was 98.4% (95% CI: 95.7%-99.4%) and 86.3% (95% CI: 79.4%-91.1%). In multivariable analysis, improved PFS and biochemical recurrence-free survival (BRFS) were observed for higher biologically effective doses with an α/β = 4 Gy (BED4) to the gross tumor volume (GTV)mean (hazard ratio [HR] 0.99; p < 0.01; HR 0.98; p < 0.001) and use of a simultaneous integrated boost (SIB; HR 0.41; p = 0.04; HR 0.40; p < 0.01; respectively). Grade 3 acute and late adverse events were rarely reported (1.0% and 0.5%, respectively). Conclusion: Stereotactic body radiotherapy of non-spinal BoM from oligometastatic prostate cancer was an effective and well-tolerated treatment. Higher GTV-BED and the use of an SIB concept were associated with more favorable PFS and BRFS, warranting confirmation in prospective studies and further standardization of target volume and dose prescription concepts.

items.title: Impact of BRCA2, BRCA1, and Other Individual Homologous Recombination Repair Alterations on Survival in Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer
items.authors: Lorente D, Tello-Velasco D, Ovejero-Sanchez M, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Objective: The clinical significance of homologous recombination repair (HRR) alterations beyond BRCA2 in advanced prostate cancer is poorly understood. We investigated the association of individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations with outcomes of patients treated with first-line therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Methods: Eligible patients from the prospective CAPTURE study underwent somatic/germ line DNA analyses using a next-generation sequencing panel including ATM, BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, CDK12, CHEK2, FANCA, HDAC2, PALB2, RAD51B, and RAD54L. Association with overall survival (OS) and radiographic progression-free survival was assessed using multivariable Cox regression models comparing individual non-BRCA2 HRR alterations to those in patients with BRCA2 alterations or without HRR alterations. Key Findings And Limitations: A total of 1010 patients were included, with BRCA2 and non-BRCA2 HRR alterations found in 122 (12%) and 191 (19%) patients, respectively. BRCA1, ATM, FANCA, HDAC2, CHEK2, CDK12, and BRIP1 alterations were observed in 19 (1.9%), 69 (6.8%), 34 (3.4%), 24 (2.4%), 23 (2.3%), 20 (2%), and 15 (1.5%) patients, respectively. Patients with ATM (hazard ratio [HR] 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.20-2.30; p = 0.002) or CHEK2 (HR 1.71; 95% CI = 1.03-2.90; p = 0.039) alterations showed improved OS compared to patients with BRCA2 alterations, with similar outcomes to patients without HRR alterations. BRCA1 (HR 0.49; 95% CI = 0.30-0.80; p = 0.004), FANCA (HR 0.61; 95% CI = 0.42-0.89; p = 0.011), and CDK12 (HR 0.57; 95% CI = 0.35-0.93; p = 0.025) were associated with worse OS compared to patients without HRR alterations, with similar outcomes to patients with BRCA2 alterations. Conclusions And Clinical Implications: Prognostic associations differ across individual HRR alterations. Although BRCA1, FANCA, or HDAC mutations were associated with a prognosis similar to that associated with BRCA2 alterations, prognosis in patients with ATM or CHEK2 alterations was similar to that in patients without HRR alterations. In the research setting, non-BRCA2 HRR alterations should be analyzed and reported as individual entities whenever possible.

items.title: Fertility Preservation in Male Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults With Cancer: A Systematic Review and Appraisal of Guidelines
items.authors: Fields E, Kaushal S, Maher S, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Advances in child, adolescent and young adult oncology have shifted the focus of cancer treatment towards quality of life. Gonadotoxicity remains a devastating late effect of treatment for some survivors. While numerous guidelines exist for fertility preservation, referral rates for fertility preservation are low. We sought to recognize and understand systemic barriers to standardized fertility care for male child, adolescent and young adults with cancer. Materials And Methods: We performed a systematic review and database search of clinical practice guidelines. Eligible guidelines included male children, adolescents, and young adults between the ages of 0-39 years diagnosed with any cancer. Appraisal was performed using the AGREE II instrument. Concordance across 28 clinical and logistical areas was analyzed to identify areas of consensus and disagreement. Results: We identified 33 guidelines globally that met inclusion criteria. Seventy-two percent of appraised guidelines were rated as "high quality". Concordance across guidelines was low overall (25%), with complete discordance in ethical and logistical domains. Key consensus items included sperm cryopreservation as a preservation method, initiation prior to gonadotoxic treatment, and inclusion of an oncologist and fertility specialist on the care team. Guidelines disagreed on the specific makeup of a multidisciplinary care team, pre-pubertal treatments, and specific ethical/logistical aspects. Conclusions: Although guidance for fertility preservation exists, it remains inconsistent and incompletely specified, particularly on ethical and logistical domains, thus limiting its clinical utility. Global efforts must prioritize standardization of logistical and ethical frameworks to enable implementation in real-world clinical practice and accelerate research in areas of controversy.

items.title: Impact of Body Mass Index on Treatment Outcomes in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer Patients Treated With Definitive Chemoradiotherapy or Radiotherapy Alone
items.authors: Pandey A, Pandey L, Mishra V, et al.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Body Mass Index (BMI) is a readily measured indicator of nutritional status; however, its impact on outcomes in head and neck cancer (HNC) patients remains understudied. This study evaluated the impact of pre‐treatment BMI on toxicities and survival in such patients. Methods This retrospective study included 212 patients of locally advanced HNC treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy alone. Patients were categorized into BMI < 25 kg/m2 and ≥ 25 kg/m2. Toxicities were assessed using CTCAE v5.0. Overall survival (OS) and locoregional control (LRC) were analyzed using the Kaplan–Meier method. Results Eighty‐six percent of patients had BMI of < 25Kg/m2. These patients experienced significantly higher rates of grade ≥ 2 mucositis, dermatitis, candidiasis, and greater need for nutritional support (44.7%; p = 0.039). Median OS and LRC were 25 and 24 months, respectively. Three‐year OS and LRC were 46.3% and 39%. BMI category, T stage, and nodal stage independently predicted OS. Conclusion BMI < 25 Kg/m2 patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or radiotherapy alone are more prone to treatment‐related toxicities and have inferior survival outcomes. Early nutritional assessment and intervention should be integrated into routine management to improve treatment outcomes.

The authors concluded that postsurgical molecular residual disease (MRD) successfully identifies patients who derive an overall survival (OS) benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT). items.abstract: To the Editor Kataoka et al reported that adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) was associated with improved overall survival (OS) in patients positive for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)−defined molecular residual disease (MRD) after curative resection of colorectal liver metastases (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.27; 95% CI, 0.08-0.88) but not in the MRD-negative subgroup (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.10-2.88). However, significance in 1 subgroup and nonsignificance in another do not establish that the effects differ; the interaction must be estimated directly.

items.title: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy for Head and Neck Cancers With Perineural Spread
items.authors: Lawless AK, Goodman CD, Wang CH, et al.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Perineural spread (PNS) in head and neck cancer (HNC) is technically challenging due to complex target volumes adjacent to critical organs. Data on stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) for PNS is scarce. Methods This retrospective study included patients treated with SBRT for PNS across two centers in the USA and Canada from 2015 to 2025. Endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression‐free survival (PFS), local control (LC), and treatment‐related toxicity. Results Thirty‐six patients were included, with median follow up of 47.5 months. Two‐year OS, PFS, and LC were 79%, 54%, and 72% respectively. Patients with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) had superior PFS and LC compared with non‐cSCC histologies. Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) accounted for the only in‐field failures. Grade ≥ 3 toxicity occurred in 22% (8/36), including grade ≥ 3 osteoradionecrosis in 6% (2/36). Temporal lobe necrosis was solely Grade 1–2 (32%). Conclusions SBRT demonstrated durable LC for selected patients with PNS, particularly cSCC, while ACC may warrant a dose‐escalated approach.

items.title: Outcomes Following Extreme Elective Nodal De-Escalation in HNSCC Treated With Curative Intent: A Community Program Experience
items.authors: Katzenberg AM, Hockstein L, Ross C, et al.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose/Objective(s) To evaluate elective nodal recurrence rates in HNSCC patients treated with extreme dose de‐escalation to 30 or 40 Gy followed by a sequential boost to gross disease or high‐risk sites. Materials/Methods Between May 2017 and May 2025, patients diagnosed with SCC of the oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx were treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy or surgery followed by adjuvant (chemo)radiotherapy. Elective nodal volumes (ENV) defined as any uninvolved adjacent, distant ipsilateral or contralateral anatomic nodal level were treated to either 30 or 40 Gy, followed by a sequential boost to the PTVp/PTVn+ or high‐risk surgical bed (PTVp+ PTVn+). A subset of 6 patients received 24–36 Gy (1.5–1.8 Gy BID) based on the Mayo‐DART regimen. Assignment to 40 Gy versus 30 Gy reflected the radiation oncologist preference based on emerging trial evidence. All cases were reviewed prospectively in a head and neck multidisciplinary conference, and treatment planning required diagnostic FDG PET‐CT fused to the planning CT. Concurrent systemic therapy was administered in 99% of patients. The primary endpoint was regional failure rate within the de‐escalated ENV. Secondary endpoints included 1‐ and 2‐year locoregional control (LRC), progression‐free survival (PFS), distant metastasis‐free survival (DMFS), and failure patterns. Results The analysis included 102 patients of whom the majority 81.4% received definitive chemoradiotherapy, 17.6% underwent surgery with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and 1% received surgery with adjuvant radiation alone. The elective nodal volume was treated to 40 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 81 patients and to 30 Gy at 2 Gy per fraction in 15 patients; the remaining 6 adjuvant patients received 24–36 Gy at 1.5–1.8 Gy twice daily per the Mayo‐DART regimen. With a median follow‐up of 26.4 months, no elective nodal failures were observed in either dose cohort. The 1‐ and 2‐year LRC rates were 93.5%. The 1‐ and 2‐year progression‐free survival (PFS) rates were 88.6% and 87.3%, respectively, while distant metastasis‐free survival (DMFS) rates were 95.0% and 95.0%, respectively. In total, 13 recurrences were recorded comprising 7 locoregional and 6 distant failures. Conclusion This represents the largest report demonstrating the efficacy of extreme dose de‐escalation to ENV's for HNSCC within an NCI designated community cancer program.…

items.title: A phase I trial of intravenous vesicular stomatitis virus expressing thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) and human interferon beta (hIFNβ) in metastatic or recurrent endometrial cancer
items.authors: Warring SK, Peng KW, Atherton PJ, et al.
items.abstract: Introduction: We report the results of a Phase I trial of intravenous (IV) vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) engineered to express human interferon beta (hIFNβ) and thyroidal sodium iodide symporter (NIS) in patients with stage IV or recurrent endometrial cancer (EC). Methods: Eligible patients with stage IV or recurrent EC with largest tumor diameter ≤ 5 cm were enrolled and received a single IV infusion of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS in a standard '3 + 3' dose escalation. Five dose-levels were planned. Primary endpoint was determination of the maximum tolerated dose (MTD). Secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, tumor response, and immune correlates. An exploratory post-hoc analysis evaluated clinical responses to subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies. Results: From 9/15/2017-1/10/23, 21 eligible patients were treated. One patient at DL2 experienced grade 3 dehydration associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and one experienced transient grade 4 asymptomatic lymphopenia, prompting protocol modification of the DLT definition. One of six patients at DL4 experienced grade 3 delirium meeting DLT criteria. Dose escalation to DL5 was not feasible because of investigational agent production limitations; MTD was not reached. The most common treatment related AEs were transient hematologic toxicities, liver enzyme elevations, and CRS. At day 29, 8 patients had progressive disease (PD); 1 entered hospice due to PD before day 29. Two patients had stable disease for at least 6 months following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS. Of the 15 patients who received subsequent ICI-based therapy following VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, 4 had durable SD with a median follow up of 40.4 (95% CI 30.4-not reached) months. Conclusions: IV VSV-hIFNβ-NIS had an acceptable safety profile in patients with advanced or recurrent EC. Further investigation of VSV-hIFNβ-NIS, particularly in combination with immune checkpoint blockade, is warranted.

items.title: Segmentation-perturbation propagation in pretrained foundation-model embeddings versus IBSI-aligned radiomics for radiologist-assessed lung-nodule malignancy classification on the LIDC-IDRI cohort
items.authors: Wanni Arachchige ICK
items.abstract: Pretrained foundation-model (FM) embeddings are proposed as robust alternatives to handcrafted radiomic features, yet whether they better withstand segmentation-mask variability, the perturbation that radiomics intraclass-correlation (ICC) filtering exists to address, has not been tested head-to-head. We quantified how segmentation-mask perturbation propagates into feature reproducibility and downstream malignancy discrimination for FM embeddings and Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI)-compliant radiomics measured on a common cohort.Approach. Two 2D FM encoders (BiomedCLIP; RadImageNet ResNet50) were compared against IBSI-compliant radiomics (3D, 107 features; 2D, 102 features) on the full eligible Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) cohort: 556 lung nodules (300 malignant, 256 benign from radiologist consensus ratings, not pathology) from 399 patients. Up to thirteen perturbed masks per nodule (up to four reader masks, eight synthetic, one Dice-calibrated) were generated, and ICC(2,1) was computed across the ten perturbation conditions available for every nodule. Malignancy classification used L2-regularized logistic regression with patient-grouped five-fold cross-validation and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals on every area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).Main results. Radiomics outperformed both foundation models on discrimination (AUC 0.940 and 0.930 for radiomics-2D/3D versus 0.833 BiomedCLIP and 0.798 RadImageNet; all radiomics-versus-FM differences significant by DeLong test, p≤10^(-7)). On perturbation stability the foundation models diverged: BiomedCLIP was statistically indistinguishable from radiomics (93.8% versus 90.2-92.5% stable features) and the most stable paradigm, whereas RadImageNet was significantly less stable (75.0%). A pre-specified diameter-stratified analysis showed the radiomics advantage narrows, and partly reverses, within size-matched strata; decision-curve analysis favoured radiomics.Significance. Two-dimensional foundation-model embeddings offered no discrimination advantage over IBSI radiomics under segmentation perturbation, and greater stability did not translate into greater accuracy. Perturbation stability is therefore decoupled from task-informativeness, and comparative benchmarks should report patient-grouped, size-stratified, calibration-aware metrics, not aggregate accuracy alone.&#xD.

items.title: Pulse-width-specific phase space modeling and reference beam characterization for UHDR electron LINAC in FLASH-RT
items.authors: Carballeira R, Gladstone D, Willy KJ, et al.
items.abstract: FLASH radiotherapy requires ultra-high dose rates (>40 Gy/s), yet commercial treatment planning systems are currently unavailable. Monte Carlo (MC) simulation offers high transport accuracy, but full-head modeling for every setup is computationally prohibitive. This work establishes a methodology for generating pulse-width-specific phase-space files for the Mobetron UHDR (9 MeV), accounting for systematic beam quality shifts caused by RF waveguide loading across pulse widths of 1.2-4.0 μs. Approach: Using GAMOS 6.2.0 MC simulations, voxelized dose distributions were post-processed via an iterative script to refine source-level parameters against experimental targets. Mean energy was optimized by matching phantom-measured R50, while energy spread was refined using surface dose and build-up gradients. Relationships derived from a mid-range 6 cm applicator were applied across clinical apertures (2.5-10 cm) to test aperture-independence. The geometric mean of experimental pulse widths (2.28 μs) was evaluated as a single reference condition. Main Results: Phase space files were generated across pulse widths and apertures. For the A6I6 reference, mean energy decreased monotonically from 9.58±0.24 to 9.04±0.24 MeV with pulse width, best described by a logarithmic model (LOO-RMSE=0.033 MeV). Energy spread increased linearly from 0.173±0.020 to 0.287±0.020 MeV (LOO-RMSE=0.005 MeV). Cross-aperture validation confirmed these shifts occur upstream of collimation. Evaluating the 2.28 μs reference predicted 9.30 MeV mean energy and 0.215 MeV energy spread, yielding depth-dose deviations ≤1.3 mm across experimental extremes and satisfying AAPM TG-106 tolerances (≤2.0 mm). Significance: This work provides pulse-width-specific phase-space characterization for Mobetron FLASH commissioning. Cross-validated regression models enable beam parameter prediction within 1.2-4.0 μs, and the 2.28 μs reference phase space streamlines routine planning while maintaining clinical accuracy.&#xD.

items.title: Clinical application of MR-Only in cyberknife stereotactic radiotherapy for brain metastases: a feasibility study
items.authors: Wang Y, Yin Z, Sheng L, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Due to the limited number of studies on MR-only stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) for brain metastases using CyberKnife in the literature, this study systematically evaluates the dose calculations and image guidance accuracy of synthetic CT (sCT) and sCT-derived digital reconstructed radiographs (sDRRs), to assess the feasibility of clinical MR-only workflow implementation in CyberKnife SRT for brain metastases. Methods: We developed a machine learning model trained on T1-weighted MR and corresponding CT images from 50 patients with brain metastases who had previously undergone CyberKnife treatment, with images from an additional 18 patients used to test the feasibility of the MR-only workflow. The Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) were used to evaluate the image quality of sCT and sDRR. For dosimetric evaluation, the sCT-based and transferred plans (namely, the original planning parameters were transferred to the sCT images for dose recalculation) was compared with the plans based on the real CT images (rCT) using DVH metrics. For image-guided positioning accuracy, the 2D errors generated by registering DRR with the digital radiography images (DRs) were converted into translational and rotational couch shifts using a geometric back-projection method, thereby assessing the consistency of positioning accuracy between the sDRRs with the rCT-derived DRRs (rDRRs). Results: The sCT images had a mean MAE of 10.08 ± 2.14 HU, a SSIM of 0.98 ± 0.01, and a PSNR of 34.73 ± 1.27 dB, and the overall sDRRs maintained high image quality (MAE: 37.36 ± 9.31 HU; SSIM: 0.95 ± 0.03; PSNR: 31.41 ± 7.14 dB). Large OARs (brainstem/eyeballs) had high DSC (> 0.80), while small OARs (lenses/optic pathway) had lower DSC. The dosimetric parameters of PTV and OARs under both planning strategies showed no statistically significant difference from the rCT-based plans (p > 0.05). When using sDRRs for image guidance, the translational errors were submillimeter, and the rotational errors had a wider distribution but mean values within robotic correction range, there was no statistical difference compared with that of the rDRRs (p > 0.05). Conclusions: The proposed model can generate accurate sCT for brain metastases, and the feasibility of the MR-only in CyberKnife SRT has been verified. Trial Registration: This study is retrospectively registered in the Clinical trial Center of Zhejiang Cancer Hospital in Jan 1th, 2024 (No. MR-33-24-003134).

items.title: 2026 Key European Guideline Changes for Metastatic Breast Cancer and Their Impact on Practice-Commentary Based on a Virtual Focus Group
items.authors: Curigliano G, Castelo-Branco L, Müller V, et al.
items.abstract: The treatment landscape for metastatic breast cancer continues to evolve rapidly, driven by advances in targeted therapies and biomarker-directed treatment decisions. The European Society for Medical Oncology Living Guidelines framework allows for timely updates reflecting emerging evidence, with the 2026 update representing significant changes across all breast cancer subtypes. An expert panel was assembled to discuss key modifications from the Living Guidelines version 1.2 to the 2026 update, examining supporting clinical trial evidence and practice implications. In hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative disease, guidelines now distinguish endocrine-sensitive from endocrine-resistant populations, with mandatory PIK3CA testing in the latter and expanded biomarker-driven second-line options. For HER2-positive disease, the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab emerges as a first-line option alongside the established taxanes-trastuzumab-pertuzumab regimen, with selection guided by disease characteristics and prior therapy. Maintenance options have also expanded, including tucatinib added to dual HER2-targeted therapy or palbociclib added to HER2-targeted therapy and endocrine therapy for HR-positive/HER2-positive disease. In triple-negative breast cancer, ADCs now move into first-line therapy for both programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-positive and PD-L1-negative/immunotherapy-ineligible populations. These advances create new implementation challenges, including comprehensive biomarker testing requirements, adverse event management necessitating multidisciplinary collaboration, and educational needs spanning the entire healthcare team. This article synthesizes expert perspectives on navigating these guideline changes, addressing barriers, and identifying unanswered questions. Successful guideline implementation requires coordinated efforts in education, infrastructure development, and adaptive strategies tailored to regional resources and expertise.

items.title: Acute Radiation Dermatitis and Recovery After Ultra-hypofractionated Versus Hypofractionated Whole-breast Radiation Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.authors: Juang S, Neiswander J, Ragupathi A, et al.
items.abstract: Background: The 2020 FAST-FORWARD trial, with 10-year outcomes presented at the 2025 ESTRO Congress, demonstrated noninferiority of 5-fraction ultra-hypofractionated radiation therapy (UHF-RT) compared with standard hypofractionated radiation therapy (HF-RT) for prevention of breast cancer recurrence. Acute radiation dermatitis remains a common toxicity with both regimens. Materials And Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 121 patients treated at a single institution between June 2022 and March 2025. 42 received UHF-RT (2600 cGy in 5 fractions ± 520 cGy boost in 1 fraction) and 79 received HF-RT (4256 cGy in 16 fractions ± 1000 cGy boost in 4 fractions). Skin toxicity was graded using the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI-CTCAE) at approximately 1 month (primary follow-up) and 3 to 6 months (secondary follow-up). Results: Toxicity grade distributions did not differ significantly at primary follow-up (P = .263). At secondary follow-up, Grade 0 toxicity was observed in 65.0% of UHF-RT patients versus 28.6% of HF-RT patients (OR 4.64, 95% CI 2.05-10.50; P < .001). Among patients with Grade 1 toxicity at primary follow-up, resolution to Grade 0 occurred in 62.5% after UHF-RT versus 21.0% after HF-RT (OR 6.28, 95% CI 2.45-16.10; P < .001). Age-adjusted sensitivity analysis supported association between UHF-RT and Grade 0 toxicity at secondary follow-up (adjusted OR 4.16, 95% CI 1.70-10.14; P = .0017). Boost-subgroup analyses were exploratory. Conclusion: UHF-RT was associated with greater resolution of acute radiation dermatitis by 3 to 6 months post-treatment compared with HF-RT following breast-conserving surgery.

items.title: Linear energy transfer optimization mitigates biological model discrepancies in carbon ion radiotherapy for pelvic osteosarcoma
items.authors: Sycheva N, Kozyra K, Seidensaal K, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Purpose: In the combined treatment of osteosarcoma with a carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) boost, large pelvic tumors are associated with significantly lower tumor control compared to craniofacial localization. This could be linked to lower dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETd) values in the target and larger uncertainties related to the model used for relative biological effectiveness (RBE) calculation. This study aimed to bridge the difference between RBE-weighted doses from two clinically used models, the local effect model I (LEM-I) and the modified microdosimetric kinetic model (mMKM), using LETd optimization. Materials And Methods: Fifteen pelvic osteosarcoma CIRT plans, initially optimized with LEM-I, were re-optimized to achieve higher target LETd while preserving target and organ at risk (OAR) dose objectives. Both dose- and LET-optimized plans were recalculated with mMKM, and dose metrics were compared across the groups. Robustness against setup and range uncertainties and changes in patient anatomy (using control CTs) was investigated. Results: LETd optimization resulted in target LETd escalation without compromising LEM-I target coverage. The LET-optimized group also demonstrated better mMKM dose coverage and a significant decrease (up to 9% of prescription) in the disparity between LEM-I and mMKM target dose. OAR doses remained largely unaffected by model choice or optimization strategy. The robustness loss with LETd optimization was minor (intra-patient dose variability increased by 0.3-2.3%) compared to the reduction in model-to-model variation. Conclusions: When adequately balanced with physical uncertainties, LETd optimization could become a useful strategy for bridging RBE model predictions and increasing the efficacy of CIRT.

items.title: Survey of Respiratory Motion Management Practices in Particle Therapy Facilities in Japan
items.authors: Miyasaka Y, Tominaga Y, Wakisaka Y, et al.
items.abstract: Respiratory motion management is essential in particle therapy because dose distributions are highly sensitive to motion. This study aimed to clarify the current implementation and technical trends of respiratory motion management in particle therapy in Japan. A questionnaire was distributed to all particle therapy facilities in Japan. Responses were received from 16 of the 26 institutions surveyed (61.5%). The survey investigated treatment sites requiring respiratory motion management, CT datasets used for treatment planning, irradiation techniques, respiratory monitoring devices, gating phase determination methods, dose evaluation approaches, and patient positioning techniques. The liver and pancreas were the treatment sites most frequently managed with respiratory motion mitigation, with 81.3% (13/16) of facilities implementing motion management for both sites. The most commonly used CT dataset for treatment planning was end-expiration phase CT (56.3%, 9/16). End-expiration respiratory-gated irradiation was the most commonly used irradiation method (87.5%, 14/16), while free-breathing and breath-hold irradiation were used less frequently. Laser-based respiratory monitoring systems were the most widely used devices for respiratory waveform acquisition (80.0%, 12/15). Determination of the irradiation phase based on tumor motion magnitude was the most commonly adopted approach (66.7%, 10/15), whereas some facilities used the same irradiation phase for all patients (20.0%, 3/15). Only a limited number of institutions explicitly evaluated dose variations associated with the interplay effect induced by respiratory motion. These findings provide an overview of current respiratory motion management practices in particle therapy facilities in Japan and may contribute to future technological development and standardization of respiratory motion management in particle therapy.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy versus standard treatment in hemato-oncology: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.authors: Szilágyi Á, Varga P, Agócs G, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has been compared with established non-CAR T treatments in several hematological malignancies, but the magnitude and consistency of benefit across diseases and comparators remain unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies in non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), and multiple myeloma (MM). Methods: 71 comparative studies evaluating CAR T-cell therapy versus standard chemoimmunotherapy (SOC), targeted therapy (TAT), transplantation, chemotherapy or donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) comparators were included. Outcomes were analyzed separately by disease entity. Treatment effects were summarized using odds ratios (ORs) for response and hazard ratios (HRs) for survival with random-effects models. Results: In NHL, largely driven by large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), CAR T-cell therapy increased response compared with SOC (OR=2.48, 95% CI=1.35-4.57) and improved overall survival (OS) (HR=0.61, 95% CI=0.48-0.78). Progression-free survival (PFS) was longer with CAR T-cells therapy than SOC in second-line LBCL, whereas no clinical advantage was observed over TAT or transplantation. In follicular lymphoma, CAR T-cells prolonged PFS versus SOC, while OS differences varied across comparators. In MM, CAR T-cells increased PFS compared with SOC or TAT (HR=0.30, 95% CI=0.11-0.77) and OS favored CAR T-cell infused patients. In ALL, OS favored CAR T-cell versus chemotherapy or DLI (HR 0.30, 95% CI=0.25-0.36) and was associated with fewer graft-versus-host disease events after transplantation. Conclusions: CAR T-cell therapy provides disease- and comparator-specific efficacy advantages without increased overall toxicity. Benefits are most consistent for PFS in LBCL and MM, however, in ALL, further comparator-specific evidence is needed.

items.title: Survival in patients with renal cell carcinoma and brain metastases: an update of the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment
items.authors: Sperduto PW, Johri F, Soliman H, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Brain metastases are a common and serious consequence for patients with renal cell carcinoma. This study aimed to determine if survival has changed since the introduction of current therapies, identify prognostic factors, update the prognostic index (the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment [GPA]) in the context of contemporary multi-modal therapies, compare outcomes with legacy cohorts, and determine whether overall survival correlates with intracranial progression-free survival. Methods: An international consortium of 21 academic institutions contributed uniformly-curated retrospective data from 1049 patients with newly-diagnosed renal cell carcinoma with brain metastases (RCC-BM) treated between Jan 1, 2016, and Dec 31, 2022. Patients treated between 1985-2007 (n=286) and 2006-15 (n=711) were considered legacy cohorts and compared to the current cohort. Significant prognostic factors for survival were identified through combined multivariable analyses and used to update the Renal GPA. Intracranial progression-free survival was defined as the interval from date of initial RCC-BM diagnosis to date of first salvage treatment. Findings: Of the 1049 patients, 773 (73·7%) patients were male and 276 (26·3%) were female; the majority (851 [81·1%]) were White, and the median age was 63·9 years (IQR 56·2-70·3). The median overall survival was 20·0 months (95% CI 18·0-23·4), with a median follow-up of 53·4 months (95% CI 50·2-56·8). Overall survival for the legacy cohorts were 9·6 months (95% CI 8-11) and 12·0 months (5-11), respectively. In combined multivariable analyses, significant prognostic factors for inferior survival were lower Karnofsky Performance Status, lower baseline serum albumin, higher number of brain metastases, and presence of extracranial metastases. These factors were incorporated into the updated Renal GPA. Median survival was 4·8 months (95% CI 3·0-8·1) for patients with GPA 0-1·0, 12·4 months (10·6-17·2) for GPA 1·5-2·0, 33·6 months (27·5-40·0) for GPA 2·5-3·0, and 51·2 months (34·1-undefined) for GPA 3·5-4·0. Median intracranial progression-free survival was 9·6 months (95% CI 8·4-10·6). The Spearman's rank correlation between intracranial progression-free survival and overall survival was moderately strong (0·74 [95% CI 0·70-0·78]; p<0·0001). Interpretation: Survival has improved compared to the legacy cohorts but varies widely by GPA.…

items.title: Tarlatamab for Treatment of Small Cell Lung Cancer in Clinical Practice: A Multicenter U.S. Retrospective Cohort Study from the ONWARD consortium
items.authors: Joshi U, Zhang B, Thompson ZJ, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Real-world data on efficacy and safety of tarlatamab in small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains limited. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 265 tarlatamab-treated patients across 11 U.S. centers in the ONWARD-SCLC consortium (11/2023-4/2025), evaluating clinical outcomes, CRS, ICANS, and impact of prophylactic medications. Results: Median age was 66 years; 87.2% had ECOG 0-1, 90.6% had de novo SCLC, and 44.5% and 39.2% had new/progressive brain and liver metastases before tarlatamab, respectively. Median prior lines of therapy were 2 (range 0-6). At a median follow-up of 4.9 months, DCR was 52.6% for evaluable SCLC cohort (all-treated: 37.9%). Median rw-PFS and rw-OS were 2.3 and 8.0 months. Median rw-PFS was 2.2 months among patients without brain metastasis versus 2.3 months among those with pre-existing brain metastasis (p=0.542). Following Cycle 1 Day 1 (C1D1), CRS occurred in 40.8% (Grade 3-4: 3.8%) and ICANS in 21.5% (Grade 3-4: 6%), with incidence declining markedly on subsequent doses. Compared to no-prophylaxis (N=237), prophylactic tocilizumab (N=19) was associated with lower CRS (5.3% vs. 43.0%; adj. p=0.017), ICANS (0% vs 22.4%; adj. p=0.041), and "prolonged hospitalization" rate (21.1% vs. 54.9%; adj. p=0.023). Multivariable analysis identified insulin-dependent diabetes, liver metastases, number of prior treatments, recent urgent care admissions, and low albumin/elevated ALT as independent predictors of worse OS. Conclusion: Tarlatamab demonstrated meaningful clinical activity in pretreated real-world cohort, including those with brain metastases. Grade ≥3 CRS and overall/grade ≥3 ICANS incidence in C1 were higher than in clinical trials. Prophylaxis patterns were characterized and warrant prospective validation.

items.title: Motion-guided semi-supervised learning with dynamic kernels for cardiac cine segmentation
items.authors: Li W, Lin G, Ding W, et al.
items.abstract: Objective: Accurate segmentation of full cardiac cine magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences is crucial for clinical diagnosis. Although deep learning models have become the standard for this task, they typically require exhaustive frame-by-frame supervision, making manual data annotation prohibitively time-consuming. Approach: To address this, we propose a novel motion-guided semi-supervised spatiotemporal framework that propagates sparse supervision from the label of the end-diastolic (ED) frame to the entire sequence. Our framework jointly optimizes motion estimation and segmentation. First, a motion decoder estimates dense displacement fields to warp the ED label, generating high-fidelity pseudo-labels for unannotated frames. Concurrently, the segmentation network employs a Temporal Kernel Segmentation (TKS) module with dynamic convolutions to adaptively capture rapid cardiac deformations, alongside a Multi-Scale Spatial Propagator (MSP) to recover fine anatomical boundaries. The motion-derived pseudo-labels directly supervise the segmentation network, ensuring temporal coherence. Main Results: Extensive experiments on a multi-center cohort from three clinical centers demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the compared methods, achieving superior segmentation accuracy and robust generalization capabilities. Significance: The proposed framework effectively mitigates the burden of manual data annotation while providing temporally coherent full-cycle cardiac analysis, holding significant potential for efficient and reliable clinical assessment of cardiovascular diseases.

items.title: Sex-disaggregated Outcomes and Safety Reporting in Perioperative Systemic Therapy for Muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review
items.authors: Mari A, Giudici S, Grobet-Jeandin É, et al.
items.abstract: Background And Objective: Sex may influence patients' response to chemotherapy or immunotherapy given before or after radical cystectomy. We reviewed all otherwise eligible prospective perioperative interventional studies, including randomized controlled trials and single-arm studies, to determine how often female enrollment, efficacy outcomes, and safety outcomes were reported separately for women and men. Methods: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched for phase 1-3 prospective interventional studies, including randomized controlled trials and single-arm studies, evaluating perioperative systemic therapy for nonmetastatic muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) between 1990 and 2024. Eligibility was based on disease setting, perioperative intervention, prospective design, and full-text availability; reporting of sex-specific outcomes was not required for inclusion and was instead coded as a review outcome. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted female enrollment and published sex-stratified efficacy or safety outcomes, and assessed risk of bias using design-appropriate tools. Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 was applied to randomized trials and the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) to noncomparative single-arm studies. Outcomes of interest were the proportion of studies reporting efficacy or adverse events (AEs) by sex, the proportion reporting formal sex-by-treatment interaction tests, and the sex-specific hazard ratios (HRs), response rates, or survival estimates provided. Key Findings And Limitations: Twenty-nine reports of 27 unique prospective perioperative trials were included, comprising 21 neoadjuvant and eight adjuvant reports, covering 6376 patients; 1140 (18%) were women. Female enrollment was 17% in neoadjuvant chemotherapy trials, 17% in neoadjuvant immunotherapy trials, 17% in adjuvant chemotherapy trials, and 22% in adjuvant immunotherapy trials. Five reports (17%) reported any sex-disaggregated efficacy outcome, whereas none reported AEs by sex. The pooled Nordic neoadjuvant series reported a female-versus-male HR >1 for overall survival (HR 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.97-1.92), although the estimate was imprecise. PURE-01 reported an imprecise female-versus-male event-free survival estimate (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.44-3.00).…

items.title: Prophylactic extended-field irradiation versus pelvic radiotherapy in high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer with radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes: a retrospective cohort study
items.authors: Shao H, Zhao Y, Cui T, et al.
items.abstract: Objective: To compare para-aortic recurrence, survival outcomes, and treatment-related toxicity between prophylactic extended-field irradiation (EFI) and pelvic radiotherapy (PRT) in patients with high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) who have radiologically negative para-aortic lymph nodes (PALNs). Methods: We retrospectively reviewed patients with FIGO 2018 stage III-IVA cervical cancer treated with definitive radiotherapy or concurrent chemoradiotherapy between December 2015 and December 2022. Eligible patients had radiologically negative PALNs and at least one high-risk feature: ≥2 positive pelvic lymph nodes, a maximum pelvic nodal short-axis diameter ≥ 1.5 cm, or pelvic sidewall involvement. Patients received EFI (n = 140) or PRT (n = 153). Survival outcomes were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression. Results: Para-aortic recurrence occurred in 2.1% of patients receiving EFI and 11.1% receiving PRT. Five-year PARFS, PFS, and DMFS were higher with EFI than with PRT (97.8% vs 88.1%, P = 0.002; 70.9% vs 58.8%, P = 0.002; and 83.7% vs 75.2%, P = 0.032, respectively). Five-year OS was 79.1% versus 68.6% (P = 0.052). In multivariable analysis, EFI remained associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.532; P = 0.002), DMFS (HR, 0.554; P = 0.036), and PARFS (HR, 0.178; P = 0.006), but not OS (HR, 0.630; P = 0.054). Grade 3-4 leukopenia was more frequent with EFI, whereas other severe toxicities were similar. Conclusions: Prophylactic EFI was associated with improved para-aortic control, PFS, and DMFS in high-risk LACC, with acceptable toxicity. These findings support further evaluation of a risk-adapted strategy for selecting patients who may benefit from prophylactic EFI.
